@grammar
A1|tenses|Present tense: now, habits and near future|15,413,431,802,822,827,1215,1606,2002,2041,2425|Spanish uses the simple present for what is true now, what you do regularly, and plans for the near future.|The Spanish present covers three English forms at once: I work, I am working and sometimes I will work.¶• **Habits and facts:** Trabajo de nueve a cinco. (I work from nine to five.)¶• **Right now:** Hoy comemos en casa de mis padres. (We are eating at my parents place today.)¶• **Planned future:** Esta noche vemos la tele. (We are watching TV tonight.) Add a time word like mañana, esta noche or el sábado and the present points to the future.¶There is no do/does in Spanish. English Do you live in Denver? is simply ¿Vives en Denver?, and I do not eat meat is simply No como carne.¶Tip for English speakers: you do not need a separate form for I am living. Vivo en Denver means both I live and I am living in Denver.
A1|tenses|Ir a + infinitive: the near future|434,474,475,872,1276,1289,2070,2472,2477,2812,2866,4070|ir a + infinitive = going to do something; ir is conjugated, the second verb stays in the infinitive.|To talk about plans and what is about to happen, use the present of **ir** + **a** + infinitive.¶T:Person¦ir¦Example//yo¦voy¦Voy a comprar pan.//tú¦vas¦Vas a llegar tarde.//él, ella, usted¦va¦Va a llover.//nosotros¦vamos¦Vamos a comer.//vosotros¦vais¦¿Vais a venir?//ellos, ustedes¦van¦Van a viajar.¶• Voy a hacer la compra. (I am going shopping.)¶• ¿Vamos a comer fuera? (Shall we eat out?) Vamos a + infinitive is also the way to say Let us...¶Do not forget the little word **a**: it is voy a hacer, not voy hacer.¶This is the most common way to speak about the future in everyday Spanish. The real future tense (hablaré) comes later.
A1|tenses|Estar + gerund: actions in progress|20,825,858,890,1237,1273,1629,1669,1670,2047|estar + -ando / -iendo says what is happening right now.|Use a present form of **estar** plus the gerund to stress that something is going on at this moment.¶T:Verb type¦Ending¦Example//-ar¦-ando¦hablando, trabajando//-er¦-iendo¦comiendo, haciendo//-ir¦-iendo¦escribiendo, viviendo¦• Estoy escribiendo un correo. (I am writing an email.)¶• Estoy aprendiendo español. (I am learning Spanish.)¶• Ya estoy durmiendo. (I am already sleeping.)¶Some gerunds change spelling: leer becomes leyendo, dormir becomes durmiendo, decir becomes diciendo.¶Tip: Spanish does not use the gerund for plans (English I am leaving tomorrow). For that use the simple present: Mañana salgo.¶Also, with verbs like ir or venir the gerund is not used to say I am going: just say Voy.
A1|tenses|Pretérito perfecto: he terminado, hemos ganado|839,1618,2003,2004,2005,2412,2426,2439|he / has / ha / hemos / han + participle (-ado, -ido) tells what has just happened; learn it as handy phrases.|In Spain the **pretérito perfecto** is the normal tense for things that happened today, recently, or that matter now.¶T:Person¦haber¦Example//yo¦he¦He terminado.//tú¦has¦¿Has comido?//él, ella, usted¦ha¦Ha ganado.//nosotros¦hemos¦Hemos perdido.//ellos, ustedes¦han¦Han llegado.¶Participles: -ar becomes **-ado** (terminar, terminado); -er and -ir become **-ido** (perder, perdido).¶• He reservado una habitación. (I have booked a room.)¶• Me he perdido. (I am lost.) The pronoun goes before he.¶• ¿Quién ha ganado? (Who won?)¶At A1, learn these as ready-made phrases. Note that haber and the participle are never separated: Ya he terminado, not He ya terminado.
A1|tenses|Quería...: the polite imperfect of querer|1201,1252,2449,2454,2455,2470,2471,2814,4055|In shops and offices, Quería... is a polite way to say I would like...|Spaniards often ask for things with the **imperfect** of querer instead of the present. It sounds softer and more polite.¶• Quería un café, por favor. (I would like a coffee, please.)¶• Quería un kilo de manzanas. (I would like a kilo of apples.)¶• Quería comprar un billete. (I would like to buy a ticket.)¶Compare:¶T:Direct¦Polite//Quiero un café.¦Quería un café.//Quiero comprar un billete.¦Quería comprar un billete.¶Even though the verb is in the past, the meaning is the present: you are asking now. Quería is the same form for yo and for él or ella (quería), so with a stranger the sentence is always about you.¶Tip: Quiero is not rude, but in a shop Quería... or ¿Me pone...? sounds friendlier.
A1|order|Subject pronouns are usually dropped|13,17,19,20,1215,3232,1603,2419,2010,1607|The verb ending shows the subject, so yo, tú, él are normally left out.|In Spanish each verb ending already shows who is doing the action, so the subject pronoun is usually **omitted**.¶• Soy de Estados Unidos. (I am from the USA.) Not Yo soy...¶• Tengo treinta años. (I am thirty.)¶• Hablo un poco de español. (I speak a little Spanish.)¶• No como carne. (I do not eat meat.)¶English speakers tend to say I... too often. In Spanish this sounds heavy.¶Keep the pronoun only when it is needed, for example:¶• with third person if it is unclear (él / ella vs. usted);¶• for contrast or emphasis (see the next rule);¶• when you just answer: ¿Quién es? Yo.¶A subject pronoun is never needed with weather or existence: Hace frío. Hay un hotel.
A1|order|Subject pronouns for emphasis and contrast|8,820,1208,1644,424,441,1265,2075|Use yo, tú, nosotros when you want to stress who is acting or to contrast people.|Subject pronouns come back when you want to **emphasise** or contrast.¶• ¿Y tú? (And you?) Used to return a question.¶• Hoy cocino yo. (I am cooking today: not you.) Pronoun after the verb for emphasis.¶• Yo quiero la sopa. (I will have the soup, and the others something else.)¶• No hay problema, yo me encargo. (No problem, I will take care of it.)¶• Mi hermano es mayor que yo. (My brother is older than me.) After que, Spanish uses yo and tú, not mí and ti.¶• ¡Tú puedes! (You can do it!)¶After prepositions, Spanish uses special forms: para mí, a ti, con él. Exceptions: entre tú y yo, según tú, and con becomes conmigo, contigo.¶Tip: usted and ustedes are more often kept than tú to be clear about politeness.
A1|order|Time words: hoy, ya, mañana, siempre|431,827,820,825,839,4007,1605,806,4006,4029,4030|Time words go at the start or end; ya and siempre sit before the verb.|Spanish word order is flexible, but a few patterns are very common.¶• **Hoy / mañana / esta noche** usually open the sentence: Hoy comemos en casa de mis padres. (Today we are eating at my parents place.) Esta noche vemos la tele. (Tonight we are watching TV.) They can also go at the end: ¿Tienes tiempo mañana? (Do you have time tomorrow?)¶• **Ya** (already, now) goes before the verb: Ya estoy durmiendo. (I am already sleeping.) Me voy ya a la cama is also possible.¶• **Ya + haber:** Ya casi he terminado. (I have almost finished.) Never put ya between haber and the participle.¶• **No** comes right before the verb, after hoy: Hoy no tengo tiempo. (I do not have time today.)¶• **Frequency words** (siempre, a veces, a menudo) go before the verb or alone: A veces voy al cine.¶Tip: in English adverbs follow the subject (I always eat). Spanish allows Siempre como or Como siempre.
A1|verbs|Regular -ar verbs in the present|19,820,840,1233,1602,1604,1606,1610,1612,1613|Drop -ar and add -o, -as, -a, -amos, -áis, -an.|Most Spanish verbs end in -ar. Remove **-ar** from the infinitive and add the endings.¶T:Person¦Ending¦hablar//yo¦-o¦hablo//tú¦-as¦hablas//él, ella, usted¦-a¦habla//nosotros¦-amos¦hablamos//vosotros¦-áis¦habláis//ellos, ellas, ustedes¦-an¦hablan¦• Hablo un poco de español. (I speak a little Spanish.)¶• Trabajo en un banco. (I work at a bank.)¶• Escucho música. (I listen to music.)¶The ending already tells you who is acting, so you rarely need yo, tú, etc.¶In Spain, vosotros is used for you (plural, informal); in Latin America people use ustedes for all groups.¶Other common -ar verbs: cocinar, estudiar, tomar, comprar, necesitar, mirar, bailar.
A1|verbs|Regular -er verbs in the present|431,827,1215,1216,2013,3232,3233|Drop -er and add -o, -es, -e, -emos, -éis, -en.|Verbs that end in -er (comer, beber, correr, aprender, leer, ver) take these endings:¶T:Person¦Ending¦comer//yo¦-o¦como//tú¦-es¦comes//él, ella, usted¦-e¦come//nosotros¦-emos¦comemos//vosotros¦-éis¦coméis//ellos, ellas, ustedes¦-en¦comen¦• No como carne. (I do not eat meat.)¶• Bebo mucha agua. (I drink a lot of water.)¶• Hoy comemos en casa de mis padres. (Today we are eating at my parents place.)¶Compare with -ar: the endings are similar, but the vowel changes from a to e (hablas, comes; hablan, comen).¶Careful: ver is slightly irregular in the yo form: veo, ves, ve, vemos, veis, ven.
A1|verbs|Regular -ir verbs in the present|15,413,432,802,829|-ir verbs are like -er verbs, except nosotros -imos and vosotros -ís.|Verbs ending in -ir (vivir, escribir, abrir, subir, decidir) use these endings:¶T:Person¦Ending¦vivir//yo¦-o¦vivo//tú¦-es¦vives//él, ella, usted¦-e¦vive//nosotros¦-imos¦vivimos//vosotros¦-ís¦vivís//ellos, ellas, ustedes¦-en¦viven¦• Vivo en Denver. (I live in Denver.)¶• Mis padres viven en Berlín. (My parents live in Berlin.)¶• Vivo en un piso pequeño. (I live in a small flat.)¶The only differences from -er verbs are **nosotros** (-imos instead of -emos) and **vosotros** (-ís instead of -éis). Everything else is identical, so you only need to memorise one extra pair.¶In Spain a flat is un piso; in much of Latin America it is un apartamento or un departamento.
A1|verbs|Ser: to be (identity, origin, profession)|12,13,43,401,406,423,424,426,1243,1603,1609,1636|ser = soy, eres, es, somos, sois, son: who or what someone is, where from, job, character.|**Ser** is irregular and must be memorised.¶T:Person¦ser//yo¦soy//tú¦eres//él, ella, usted¦es//nosotros¦somos//vosotros¦sois//ellos, ellas, ustedes¦son¦Use ser for:¶• **Identity:** Este es mi amigo Tom. A1|verbs|Estar: location and state|6,7,407,408,421,422,445,801,808,813,815,821,824|estar = estoy, estás, está, estamos, estáis, están: where something is and how someone feels.|**Estar** is irregular in the yo form (estoy) and carries a written accent in estás, está and están.¶T:Person¦estar//yo¦estoy//tú¦estás//él, ella, usted¦está//nosotros¦estamos//vosotros¦estáis//ellos, ellas, ustedes¦están¦Use estar for:¶• **Location:** ¿Dónde está el baño? (Where is the bathroom?) Estoy en casa. (I am at home.)¶• **Health and mood:** ¿Cómo está usted? (How are you? formal) Estoy cansado. (I am tired.)¶• **Results and states:** La comida está lista. (Dinner is ready.) Estoy casado. (I am married.)¶Tip: even for permanent things, if it is a position in space, use estar: Berlín está en Alemania. (Berlin is in Germany.)
A1|verbs|Ser vs. estar: the basic split|13,406,426,1603,3616,808,824,3632,2407,801,407,821|ser = what someone or something is like; estar = where it is and how it is right now.|Both verbs mean to be, but they are not interchangeable.¶T:Use ser for¦Use estar for//identity and job: Soy ingeniero.¦location: Estoy en casa.//origin: Soy de Estados Unidos.¦temporary state: Estoy cansado.//character: Es muy majo. (He is very nice.)¦mood and health: Estoy tranquilo.//time and date: Hoy es lunes.¦results: La comida está lista.¶• Es aburrido. (That is boring: its nature.) vs. Está aburrido. (He is bored: right now.)¶• ¿Está lejos? (Is that far?) Distance is a location, so estar.¶Some adjectives change meaning: ser listo (clever) vs. estar listo (ready); ser aburrido (boring) vs. estar aburrido (bored).¶Rule of thumb: Ser = what it IS, estar = where and how it is NOW.
A1|verbs|Tener: to have, age and common expressions|16,17,403,404,405,409,411,412,418,442,828,1203,1204,3215,1605,1645|tener = tengo, tienes, tiene...; Spanish uses tener for age, hunger, thirst, cold.|**Tener** is irregular: tengo, tienes, tiene, tenemos, tenéis, tienen (stem e becomes ie, and yo is tengo).¶• **Possession:** Tengo dos hermanos. (I have two brothers.) ¿Tienes hijos? (Do you have children?)¶• **Age:** ¿Cuántos años tienes? Tengo treinta años. (I am thirty years old.) Never say Soy treinta.¶• **Feelings and sensations:** Tengo hambre. (I am hungry.) Tengo sed. (I am thirsty.) Tengo frío. (I am cold.)¶• **Time:** No tengo tiempo. (I do not have time.)¶Tip for English speakers: where English uses to be (I am hungry, I am cold, I am 30), Spanish uses tener plus a noun. Tengo mucha hambre: use mucho, not muy, because hambre is a noun.
A1|verbs|Hay: there is / there are|830,1235,1644,2442,2813,2840,445,801,815,2407|hay = there is or there are; it never changes. Use estar for a specific known thing.|**Hay** comes from haber and is used for the existence of things, singular or plural. It never changes.¶• ¿Hay ascensor? (Is there an elevator?)¶• ¿Hay un hotel por aquí? (Is there a hotel around here?)¶• ¿Dónde hay un cajero? (Where is there an ATM?)¶• No hay problema. (There is no problem.)¶**Hay vs. está:**¶• Hay goes with an indefinite thing: un hotel, pan, ascensor. ¿Hay un hotel por aquí?¶• Está / están goes with a definite thing: el, la, mi, tu. ¿Dónde está el baño? ¿Dónde están mis llaves? (Where are my keys?)¶Hay does not go with a definite noun: say ¿Dónde está el hotel? and not ¿Dónde hay el hotel?¶Tip: English there is/there are both become hay.
A1|verbs|Ir: to go (voy, vas, va)|2419,2010,1607,2007,809,806,4039,2038,2026|ir = voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van; use a for the destination, en for the vehicle.|**Ir** is completely irregular.¶T:Person¦ir//yo¦voy//tú¦vas//él, ella, usted¦va//nosotros¦vamos//vosotros¦vais//ellos, ellas, ustedes¦van¦• Voy a Berlín. A1|verbs|Reflexive verbs: me llamo, me levanto|9,10,416,436,807,822,823,806,809,1616,3221,2441|Reflexive verbs need me, te, se, nos, os, se before the verb: me llamo, te levantas.|With reflexive verbs the action returns to the subject. A1|verbs|Gustar: me gusta, me gustan|1217,1218,1219,1220,1635,2001,2006,2019,2021,2025,2034,2822,2823,3610|Gustar agrees with the thing liked: me gusta + singular or infinitive, me gustan + plural.|Gustar literally means to be pleasing to. A1|verbs|Imperative basics: polite commands|816,817,810,2039,2404,2405,2406,3274,3275,76|Tú commands are the él form (cierra); usted commands use the -e / -a ending (siga, gire).|To give an order, instruction or invitation, Spanish uses the imperative.¶• **Tú (informal):** use the él/ella form of the present for affirmative regular verbs: Cierra la puerta. (Close the door.) Abre la ventana. (Open the window.) ¡Espera! (Wait!) ¡Sigue! (Keep going!)¶• **Usted (formal):** -ar verbs take **-e**, -er and -ir verbs take **-a**: Gire a la izquierda. (Turn left.) Siga todo recto. (Go straight on.) Abra la boca. (Open your mouth.) Siéntese. (Sit down.)¶Irregular tú commands you need soon: ven, pon, sal, haz, di, ve, ten.¶Add **por favor** to be polite: Cierra la puerta, por favor.¶A reflexive pronoun is attached to an affirmative command: siéntese, cuídate. The accent keeps the stress where it was: Cuídate mucho.
A1|modal|Querer + infinitive: wants and orders|441,1205,1231,1241,2841,2083,2084,1208|quiero / quieres / quiere + infinitive = want to do; also used to order food.|**Querer** (to want) is followed directly by an infinitive; there is no word like to between them.¶• Quiero comprar esto. (I want to buy this.)¶• Queremos pedir. (We would like to order.)¶• Quiero pagar. (I would like to pay.)¶• ¿Quieres comer con nosotros? (Do you want to eat with us?)¶• ¿Qué quieres beber? (What would you like to drink?)¶Querer is a stem-changing verb: quiero, quieres, quiere, queremos, queréis, quieren.¶With a noun it is used to order: Yo quiero la sopa. (I will have the soup.)¶Careful: Te quiero means I love you. With people, querer is affection; to want to have something, add a thing: Quiero un café. Compare with Quería un café for a politer request.
A1|modal|Poder + infinitive: can, may, requests|2427,2438,3237,50,55,85,1253,1648,847,871|puedo / puedes / puede + infinitive = can; ¿Puede...? asks for help or permission.|**Poder** (can, to be able to) is followed by an infinitive. It is a stem-changing verb: puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, podéis, pueden.¶• **Ability:** No puedo dormir. (I cannot sleep.)¶• **Permission:** ¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta? (Can I pay by card?)¶• **Requests:** ¿Puedes ayudarme? (Can you help me?) With a stranger or a person older than you, use usted: ¿Me puede ayudar? (Can you help me?)¶• **Questions about possibility:** ¿Dónde puedo cambiar dinero? (Where can I change money?)¶Pronouns can go before poder (¿Me puede ayudar?) or be attached to the infinitive (¿Puede ayudarme?). Both are correct.¶Tip: for skills (can swim, can drive) Spanish uses saber: Sé nadar.
A1|modal|Tener que + infinitive: have to|846,850,1271,1664,2447,2448,3256,3259,3270,3271,111|tener que + infinitive = must, have to; the que is essential.|To express obligation, use a form of **tener** + **que** + infinitive.¶• Tengo que ir al dentista. (You have to book.) It means that anybody should.¶Do not forget que: Tengo ir is wrong. Compare tener + noun (Tengo dos hermanos) with tener que + verb.
A1|modal|Necesitar + noun or infinitive|1643,2031,2809,2831,3210,3219,3241,3397,1272|necesito + noun or infinitive; no preposition needed.|**Necesitar** (to need) is a regular -ar verb. It is more direct than querer.¶Compare: necesitar = need, querer = want.
A1|articles|Definite articles: el, la, los, las|801,804,812,814,837,445,833,823,1217,1236|Spanish has four "the" words: el, la, los, las. (I like cheese.)¶• Body parts take the article, not "my": Me lavo **los** dientes. (I brush my teeth.)¶Tip for English speakers: you cannot drop the article before a noun the way English does with "I like cheese". Learn each noun together with its article (el baño, la cama).
A1|articles|Indefinite articles: un, una, unos, unas|404,435,802,803,841,1201,1207,2412,2031,2835|un and una mean "a/an"; unos and unas mean "some". (I need running shoes.)¶Ordering in a cafe or hotel, you simply say un/una plus the noun: **Una** cerveza, por favor. (A beer, please.) Remember: un is masculine, una is feminine, and "a" in English never changes.
A1|articles|Gender of nouns: -o, -a, -ción, -dad|801,837,1217,813,2401,1236,804,3611,2414,2412|Most nouns in -o are masculine and in -a feminine; -ción, -sión, -dad and -tad are feminine.|Every Spanish noun has a gender, and the ending usually tells you which.¶T:Ending¦Gender¦Example//-o¦masculine¦el queso, el baño, el pan//-a¦feminine¦la cama, la puerta, la música//-ción, -sión¦feminine¦la habitación, la estación//-dad, -tad¦feminine¦la ciudad, la verdad//-e or consonant¦learn each one¦el postre, la luz, el hotel¶• ¿Dónde está **la** estación de tren? A1|articles|Contractions al and del (a + el, de + el)|1607,2010,2001,2008,2022,838,1641,2409,2029,2044|a + el becomes al and de + el becomes del. A1|articles|Gender exceptions: el agua, el día, la mano|866,1206,2086,1605,2451,2461,2478,4026|Some nouns break the -o/-a pattern: el día, el mapa, el problema are masculine; la mano, la foto are feminine.|A few very common nouns do not follow the ending rule.¶T:Masculine in -a¦Feminine in -o//el día (the day)¦la mano (the hand)//el mapa (the map)¦la foto (the photo)//el problema, el idioma¦la moto (the motorbike)¶• Hoy tengo **el día** libre. A1|articles|No article: jobs, nationalities and tener + noun|1603,1636,1609,1602,433,2432,1203,1204,4007,1218|After ser with a job or nationality, and in tener hambre/sed, Spanish uses no article.|English says "I am an engineer"; Spanish leaves out the article when you simply name a job, role or nationality.¶• Soy ingeniero. A1|nouns|Plural of nouns: -s and -es|445,823,833,2031,2835,3218,413,815,828,2415,403,2818|Add -s after a vowel (niño, niños) and -es after a consonant (llave, llaves; habitación, habitaciones).|T:Singular ends in¦Plural¦Example//vowel¦add **-s**¦niño → niños, zapato → zapatos//consonant¦add **-es**¦papel → papeles, mes → meses//-ión¦-iones (accent drops)¦habitación → habitaciones¶The article and the adjective change too: **los** zapatos nuevos, **las** habitaciones pequeñas.¶• ¿Dónde están **los niños**? A1|nouns|Plural spelling changes and special plurals|2018,2081,3257,3612,1633,3267,2418,3218|z becomes c before -es (vez, veces); weekdays lunes to viernes do not change; vacaciones and gafas are plural.|A few plural patterns need attention.¶• **z → c** before -es: una vez → dos **veces**; el lápiz → los lápices. A1|pronouns|Subject pronouns: yo, tú, él, ella, nosotros, vosotros|8,424,820,1208,1257,1265,1277,1644,2075|Spanish usually drops subject pronouns; use yo, tú, él... only to stress or contrast who does something.|T:¦singular¦plural//1st¦**yo**¦**nosotros / nosotras**//2nd (informal)¦**tú**¦**vosotros / vosotras**//3rd¦**él / ella**¦**ellos / ellas**//formal¦**usted**¦**ustedes**¶The verb ending already shows the person, so Spanish normally leaves the pronoun out: Vivo en Denver. A1|pronouns|Tú vs. usted: informal and formal you|6,10,16,2427,2805,2830,3213,1242,2824,1219|Use tú with friends, family and young people; use usted (with a third-person verb) with strangers, elders, officials.|Spanish has two ways to say "you" to one person.¶T:¦informal¦formal//pronoun¦**tú**¦**usted**//verb form¦2nd person: tienes¦3rd person: **tiene**//asking¦¿Cómo estás?¦¿Cómo **está usted**?¶• ¿Cómo te llamas? / ¿Cuántos años tienes? A1|pronouns|Possessives before a noun: mi, tu, su, nuestro|43,401,412,413,421,431,436,438,427,430|mi, tu, su come before the noun and add -s for plural owned things (mi hijo, mis hijos); nuestro changes for gender too.|Possessives agree with the thing owned, not with the owner.¶T:Owner¦one thing¦several things//I¦mi¦mis//you (tú)¦tu¦tus//he / she / you (usted)¦su¦sus//we¦nuestro / nuestra¦nuestros / nuestras//you all (vosotros)¦vuestro / vuestra¦vuestros / vuestras¶• Este es **mi** amigo Tom. A1|pronouns|Demonstratives: este, esta, esto, eso|43,401,1221,2441,2437,40,1225,3608,2841,1230|este/esta (near you) and ese/esa (farther) agree with the noun; esto and eso are neuter for unnamed things.|Demonstratives point to things. A1|pronouns|Gustar and doler: me gusta, me duele|1217,1218,1219,2001,2006,3202,3208,3218,3226,2822|With gustar and doler the thing liked or aching is the subject: Me gusta el queso, Me duelen las muelas.|Gustar does not work like "to like". A1|preps|En vs. a: where you are and where you go|15,803,1604,2444,829,2419,806,809,1607,2007|Use en for being somewhere or for transport; use a for going to a place (ir a, llegar a).|T:Preposition¦Meaning¦Example//**en**¦location (in, at, on)¦Vivo **en** Denver. A1|preps|De: origin, possession and description|13,2440,12,427,431,838,2409,2029,1641,2874|de shows where you are from, who owns something and what something belongs to: Soy de Canadá, la parada del autobús.|The preposition **de** is one of the most common words in Spanish.¶• **Origin**: Soy **de** Canadá. A1|preps|Para: purpose, recipient and destination|1209,1226,1232,2030,2402,2415,2833,3397,3640|para introduces who something is for, its purpose, or a destination: Para mí, una pizza; una mesa para dos.|A1 learners mostly need para for these uses:¶• **For someone**: Para mí, una pizza. (A ticket to Munich, please.)¶• **Para + infinitive** = in order to: Hace buen tiempo **para** correr. (The weather is good for running.)¶Para llevar means "to go" (take away) and para tomar aquí "for here".¶Do not mix it up with por, which you already know from por favor. At this level, learn them as fixed chunks: por favor, por la mañana, para mí.

A1|preps|Personal a before people|430,434,3213,478,82,451,477|When the direct object is a specific person or pet, put a before it: Llamo a mi madre.|In Spanish, the direct object that is a specific person (or a loved pet) is introduced by **a**. A1|conj|Y / e: joining words and sentences|2422,2423,4003,4004,861,1272,4069,4087,1727,3309|y means and; before a word starting with i- or hi- it becomes e.|**Y** (and) joins words, phrases and sentences.¶• Ida y vuelta, por favor. A1|conj|O / u: choosing between options|2422,1248,1335,1373,2509,3829,4291,4295|o means or; before a word starting with o- or ho- it becomes u.|**O** (or) offers a choice or an alternative.¶• ¿Solo ida o ida y vuelta? A1|conj|Pero: but|111,159,286,537,653,3462,4815,5559,6046|pero introduces a contrast; it is always written with a comma before it.|**Pero** (but) joins two ideas that contrast or limit each other.¶• Estoy bastante estresado, pero por lo demás bien. A1|neg|Negation with no|21,42,832,1215,1216,1218,1645,2408,2809,2839,3231,3237|Put no directly before the verb; there is no do-support.|To make a sentence negative, put **no** directly before the verb.¶• Hablo español. → No hablo español. A1|numbers|Days, months and dates|4008,4009,4010,4011,439,4041,3612,2041,4014,1664|Days and months are lowercase and masculine; use el for a day (el lunes), los for repeated days (los lunes), and en for months.|T:Days (el...)¦Months (en...)//lunes, martes, miércoles¦enero, febrero, marzo//jueves, viernes¦abril, mayo, junio//sábado, domingo¦julio, agosto, septiembre, octubre, noviembre, diciembre¶• ¿Qué día es hoy? **Hoy es** lunes. A1|particles|Por favor, vale, claro, perdón: everyday words|22,23,24,27,28,29,30,32,804,805,816,1201,1202,1206|Learn these little words: por favor, gracias, perdón, lo siento, vale, claro.|These short words are used all day in Spain.¶• **Por favor** (please) goes at the end or the beginning: Cierra la puerta, por favor. A1|punct|Question and exclamation marks: ¿ ? ¡ !|1,2,10,36,2024,1213,3615,3629,2401,2805,25,44|Spanish opens every question and exclamation with an upside-down mark: ¿Cómo te llamas? ¡Qué rico!|Spanish writes a mark at both ends of a question or exclamation: **¿...?** and **¡...!**¶• ¿Cómo te llamas? A1|punct|Written accents (tildes) and the letter ñ|813,2401,1627,3210,840,8,411,1219,445,34,1201,35|Words ending in a vowel, n or s stress the second-last syllable; a tilde marks any exception: habitación, número, qué.|Most words follow two simple rules without a written accent:¶• words ending in a **vowel, -n or -s** are stressed on the second-last syllable: **ca**sa, **ha**blan, **lu**nes¶• words ending in any **other consonant** are stressed on the last syllable: ciu**dad**, hablar, pa**pel**¶A tilde (´) shows where the rule is broken:¶• ¿Dónde está la estación? A1|style|Asking politely: ¿Me puede...?, Quería..., por favor|1201,1231,1241,1256,49,50,2423,816,2427|Soften requests with por favor, Quería, ¿Podría...? and by using usted.|In shops, restaurants and offices, how you ask matters. A2|tenses|Perfecto with ya, todavía no, nunca, alguna vez|1288,2479,839,2865,2517,1702,903,2484|With ya, todavía no, nunca and alguna vez, Spaniards use the perfecto: Ya he comido; Todavía no ha llegado.|Some time words pair naturally with the **pretérito perfecto** because they link the past to the present moment.¶T:Word¦meaning¦example//**ya**¦already / yet¦¿**Ya has comido**? (I met a new friend.)//Specific past moment¦**indefinido**¦Ayer **corrí** diez kilómetros. (Yesterday I ran ten kilometers.)¶• Experience up to now: **Ya he estado** en París. Once you add a finished date, switch: **Estuve** en París en 2019.¶• Ordering something online and it is still in your life: **Lo he pedido** por internet.¶• Tip: this is a Spain-vs-Latin-America difference. In much of Latin America people use the indefinido for recent events (Hoy comí) where Spaniards say Hoy **he comido**.
A2|tenses|Pretérito imperfecto: forms and habits|4067,1259,1258,4108,98,117,119,130|Imperfecto (-aba, -ía) describes how things used to be: habits, descriptions, ongoing background.|The **imperfecto** talks about the past without caring when it began or ended. Use it for habits, descriptions and what was going on.¶T:Person¦hablar¦comer / vivir//yo¦habl**aba**¦com**ía**//tú¦habl**abas**¦com**ías**//él/ella¦habl**aba**¦com**ía**//nosotros¦habl**ábamos**¦com**íamos**//vosotros¦habl**abais**¦com**íais**//ellos¦habl**aban**¦com**ían**¶• Only three verbs are irregular: **ser** (era, eras, era, éramos, erais, eran), **ir** (iba, ibas, iba, íbamos, ibais, iban) and **ver** (veía...).¶• Habit: **Antes vivía** en Viena. (I used to live in Vienna.)¶• Description: **Era** pequeño y **tenía** un perro. (I was little and had a dog.) ¿Qué tal **estaba** todo? (Did you enjoy it?)¶• Ongoing action: ¿Por dónde **íbamos**? A2|tenses|Imperfecto vs. indefinido: background and event|4108,3016,2896,4120,4111,2487,4072,2486|Imperfecto sets the scene (was happening); indefinido tells what happened (a finished event).|Stories usually mix both tenses. The **imperfecto** paints the background; the **indefinido** moves the story forward.¶T:Imperfecto¦Indefinido//description, mood, weather¦completed action//habit, repeated action¦single event//action in progress¦action that interrupts or ends//no clear start or end¦clear start or end¶• No **estaba** en casa cuando **vino** el repartidor. (I wasn't home when the courier came.) The first verb is the situation, the second the event.¶• Cuando **era** pequeño, **tenía** un perro. (When I was little I had a dog.) Both are background, so both are imperfecto.¶• **Llovió** todo el rato. (It rained the whole time.) With a limited stretch of time the indefinido fits: todo el rato, dos semanas, tres horas.¶• Al principio **fue** difícil. (At the beginning it was hard.) A summary of a whole phase uses the indefinido.¶• Ya **estaba** roto cuando lo **compré**. (It was already broken when I bought it.)¶• Tip: ask yourself "Is it a snapshot or a movie scene?" Snapshot of an event: indefinido; scene: imperfecto.

A2|tenses|Estar + gerundio: actions in progress|20,841,1237,1629,858,890,2047,2061,825,500|Estar + -ando/-iendo says what is happening right now: Estoy leyendo un libro.|Use **estar + gerundio** for an action that is in progress at the moment of speaking or in this period of time.¶T:Verb type¦gerund¦example//-ar¦-**ando**¦Estoy habl**ando**, trabaj**ando**//-er / -ir¦-**iendo**¦Estoy com**iendo**, viv**iendo**¶• Estoy **leyendo** un libro. A2|tenses|Llevar + time + gerundio; acabar de + infinitive|1297,1668,625,878,505,2096|Llevo tres años trabajando = I have been working for three years; Acabo de comer = I have just eaten.|Two handy verb phrases for time and recent events.¶**1. llevar + time + gerundio** (how long something has been going on, up to now):¶• **Llevo** tres años **trabajando** aquí. A2|tenses|Present tense for near future and promises|1630,4199,1661,1678,1672,862,4039,1691|In everyday Spanish the present often means the future: Te llamo luego; Ahora vuelvo.|Spanish uses the **present tense** for plans and promises that are close or fixed, just as English says "I'm seeing him tomorrow".¶• **Te llamo** luego. (I'll call you later.) **Te llamo** esta noche. (I'll call you tonight.)¶• **Ahora vuelvo**. (I'll be right back.) **Le devuelvo** la llamada. (I'll call you back.)¶• **Nos mudamos** el mes que viene. (We're moving next month.) La semana que viene **me cojo** vacaciones. (I'm taking vacation next week.)¶• Mañana **te digo** algo. (I'll tell you something tomorrow.)¶• A future time word (luego, mañana, el mes que viene, esta noche) makes the meaning clear, so no future form is needed.¶• Use this for plans and offers; use **ir a** or the **futuro** for predictions: Va a llover.¶• Tip: after si the present is also used for the future: Si **llueve**, me quedo en casa. A2|order|Object pronouns: before the verb or on the infinitive|50,85,473,1682,2461,2844,2854,2880,2905,3691,2866|Pronouns go before a conjugated verb, but attach to the end of an infinitive or gerund (or go before the first verb).|Direct and indirect object pronouns (**me, te, lo, la, nos, os, los, las, le, les**) normally stand **before the conjugated verb**: **Lo** he pedido por internet. A2|order|Question word order: no do-support|12,14,438,445,801,838,1611,1626,848,488|Spanish questions use a question word + verb, then the subject: ¿Dónde vive tu hermano?|English adds "do/does" and keeps the subject before the verb. (Where is the bathroom?)¶• Do not say ¿Dónde tu hermano vive? or ¿Cuándo tu cumpleaños es?¶• Yes/no questions keep the statement word order; the intonation rises and the marks ¿ ? frame the question: ¿**Tienes** hermanos? or ¿**Tienes tú** hermanos? (with emphasis).¶• Words with prepositions stay together at the front: ¿**A quién le toca** fregar hoy? (Whose turn is it to do the dishes?) ¿**De dónde eres**? (Where are you from?)¶• Every question word carries an accent: **qué, quién, cuándo, dónde, cómo, cuánto, cuál**.¶• ¿Cómo se llama tu novia? (What's your girlfriend's name?)

(Don't worry.) **No te preocupes por eso**. (Don't worry about it.)¶• **No te olvides** de echarle sal al agua. (Don't forget to salt the water.)¶• **No te lo tomes a mal**, pero tengo que cancelar. A2|verbs|Saber vs. conocer|42,3675,1729,11,204,454,455,478,491,202|Saber = know facts or how to do something; conocer = be acquainted with people, places, things.|Both mean "to know", but they are not interchangeable.¶T:Verb¦use¦example//**saber** (sé, sabes, sabe...)¦facts, information; skills (+ infinitive); whether (+ si)¦**No lo sé.** (I don't know.) **Sé** trabajar bajo presión. (I can work under pressure.)//**conocer** (conozco, conoces...)¦be acquainted with a person or place; meet for the first time¦¿De qué **conoces** a Lisa? (How do you know Lisa?)¶• **Nos conocemos** desde el colegio. (We've known each other since school.) **Nos conocimos** en la universidad. (We met at university.)¶• In the indefinido and perfecto conocer means "to meet": **He conocido** a un amigo nuevo. ¿Cómo os **conocisteis**? Encantado de **conocerte**.¶• Saber + infinitive = know how to / can: **Sé** nadar. (I can swim.) This is different from poder, which is about possibility.¶• The personal **a** comes before a person after conocer: **Conozco a** tu hermano; no a before a thing: **Conozco** Madrid.¶• Both are irregular in yo: sé, conozco.
A2|verbs|Tener expressions: tengo hambre, tengo prisa|1203,1204,4088,3671,3252,3408,484,3248,3806|Spanish uses tener where English uses be: tengo hambre, sed, prisa, razón, años, miedo.|Many states that English expresses with "to be" use **tener + noun** in Spanish. A2|modal|Poder: ability, permission and requests|50,85,847,871,1253,2458,2438,2475,1648,2073|Poder (puedo, puedes, puede) + infinitive: can, may, and the usual way to ask someone to do something.|**Poder** is stem-changing (o > ue): puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, podéis, pueden. (What is there to do here?)¶• **Permission:** ¿**Puedo** pagar con tarjeta? (Can I pay by card?) ¿**Puedo** dejar el equipaje aquí? (Can I leave my luggage here?)¶• **Requests:** ¿**Puedes** cerrar la ventana? (Can you close the window?) ¿**Me puedes** enviar el archivo? (Can you send me the file?)¶• **Not being able:** ¡**No puedo** más! (I can't go on!)¶• Pronouns can go before poder or after the infinitive: ¿**Me puedes** ayudar? = ¿**Puedes ayudarme**?¶• Use **puede** (usted) with strangers: ¿**Me puede** ayudar? A2|modal|Querer and quería: wants and polite wishes|441,1205,1231,1241,1201,1252,2449,2454,2470,4055|Quiero = I want; quería = I would like (polite); queremos pedir = we would like to order.|**Querer** (e > ie): quiero, quieres, quiere, queremos, queréis, quieren. (What would you like to drink?)¶• **Quería** (imperfecto) is the polite form for shops, hotels and offices, even though it is a request about now: **Quería** un café, por favor. **Quería** un asiento de ventanilla. **Quería comprar** un billete.¶T:Situation¦polite¦direct//ordering¦**Quería** un café¦Quiero un café//asking¦**Quería pedir** cita¦Quiero una cita¶• Avoid sounding blunt: **Quiero** un café works among friends but sounds demanding to a waiter, so add por favor or use quería / me gustaría.¶• Te **quiero** (I love you) is a different meaning of querer with a person.¶• Querer que + subjunctive: Quiero **que vengas**. A2|modal|Tener que + infinitive: obligation|110,111,897,901,910,846,850,1271,2905,2921|Tener que + infinitive says what you must do: Tengo que ahorrar.|**Tener que + infinitive** expresses personal obligation or necessity. A2|modal|Hay que + infinitive: general necessity|1004,913,2509,2757,3593,785,3389,2386|Hay que + infinitive = one must / it is necessary; it has no subject and never changes.|**Hay que + infinitive** expresses a general obligation or need that does not belong to a particular person (like "one has to", "you need to", "it is necessary to"). (There's no need to worry.)¶T:Structure¦meaning¦example//**hay que** + inf¦general need¦Hay que reservar.//**tener que** + inf¦personal duty¦**Tengo que** reservar.//**deber** + inf¦should, moral duty¦**Debes** reservar.¶• Compare: Hay que salir temprano (it's necessary, for everyone) vs. Tengo que salir temprano (I personally must).¶• Reflexive pronouns attach to the infinitive: Hay que **ponerse** una dosis de recuerdo.

A2|articles|Days of the week with el and los|450,615,2202,4048,4052,4203,4204|Use el + day for one particular day, los + day (plural) for every week.|In Spanish you say **el** before a day of the week when you mean one specific day. A2|articles|Article with body parts and possessions|2064,3202,3203,3208,3209,3218,3224,3225,3236|Use the article, not mi/tu, with body parts: me duele la cabeza.|English says "my head hurts". A2|adjectives|Comparatives: más/menos ... que|425,49,216,2903,2904,2923,4110,4046,1819,1314|Use más/menos + adjective or adverb + que: más barato que, más tarde que.|To compare, put **más** (more) or **menos** (less) before the adjective or adverb and **que** for "than".¶T:Structure¦Example//más + adj. + que¦Mi hermana es **más** pequeña **que** yo.//más + adv. + que¦Gano **más que** antes.//menos + noun + que¦Como **menos** azúcar **que** antes.¶En las rebajas todo está **más barato**. (Everything is cheaper at the sale.)¶Lo he visto **más barato** por internet. (I saw it cheaper online.)¶Con el tiempo se hace **más fácil**. (I already feel better.)¶Podría ser **peor**. (It could be worse.)¶El dolor va a **peor**. (The pain is getting worse.)¶• **Mejor** and **peor** have the same form for masculine and feminine; the plural is **mejores, peores**: **las mejores ideas**.¶• Do not say más bueno or más mal.¶• **Mayor** and **menor** mean older and younger, mainly for people (**mi hermano mayor**). For size, use **más grande, más pequeño**.¶• **Mejor** alone also means "it would be better to": **Mejor por la mañana.** (Preferably in the morning.)
A2|adjectives|Superlatives: el más, la mejor|605,1287,2460,2611,2474,2500,519,3371|Article + más/menos/mejor + adjective, followed by de: el más pequeño de la familia.|To say "the most" or "the -est", use the definite article before más or menos, and **de** for "in/of".¶T:Structure¦Example//el/la/los/las + más + adj.¦Es **el más** pequeño **de** la familia.//el/la + mejor / peor¦Es **la mejor** forma de llegar.//el/la + más + adj. + noun¦la gasolinera **más** cercana¶¿Dónde está la gasolinera **más cercana**? A2|adjectives|Very much: the -ísimo ending|1247,1260,1419,2105,3290,3803,3827|Adding -ísimo to an adjective means "extremely": bueno becomes buenísimo.|Spanish has a very common way of saying "very, extremely": drop the final vowel and add **-ísimo, -ísima, -ísimos, -ísimas**. A2|adjectives|Shortened adjectives: buen, mal, gran|38,39,81,2030,2088,2885,3641,3642,423,681|Before a masculine singular noun bueno and malo lose -o: buen día, mal humor.|Some adjectives are shortened when they stand **before a masculine singular noun** (apócope). A2|adjectives|Adjective agreement and position|423,802,858,1624,1673,2878,478,821,824,1228,1275,3678|Adjectives agree in gender and number and usually follow the noun: un piso pequeño.|Spanish adjectives change to match the noun (masculine/feminine, singular/plural) and normally come **after** the noun.¶T:Ending¦Masc. sing.¦Fem. sing.¦Plural//-o / -a¦un piso nuevo¦una casa nueva¦pisos nuevos, casas nuevas//-e¦un coche grande¦una familia grande¦grandes//consonant¦un test fácil¦una tarea fácil¦fáciles¶Vivo en un piso **pequeño**. A2|preps|En vs a: where you are and where you go|808,809,1607,1608,2480,2482,431,2491|Use en for location and means of transport, a for movement towards a place.|**En** says where something is or how you travel. **A** shows movement towards a destination.¶T:Idea¦Preposition¦Example//location¦**en**¦Estoy **en** la oficina.//direction¦**a**¦Me voy **a** casa.//means of transport¦**en**¦Fui **en** tren.//on foot¦**a**¦Voy **a** pie.¶Estuvimos dos semanas **en** España. (We were in Spain for two weeks.)¶Nos vamos **a** la playa. (We are going to the beach.)¶Voy **al** trabajo en autobús. (I take the bus to work.)¶• **A + el** always contracts to **al**: voy **al** cine. (**De + el** becomes **del**.)¶• Verbs of movement (ir, llegar, volver) use **a**; verbs of staying (estar, vivir, quedarse) use **en**.¶• Question forms: **¿Dónde estás?** (location) vs **¿Adónde vas?** (direction).¶• English "I go by bus" uses "by"; Spanish uses **en**, not por.
A2|preps|Por vs para: first uses|452,465,1283,2477,486,1284,1671,3723|Para gives purpose, destination or recipient; por gives cause, means and time of day.|**Por** and **para** both translate as "for" and cause trouble. (I talk on the phone with my mother.)¶¡Gracias **por** la invitación! (Thanks for the invitation!)¶• Rule of thumb: **para** looks forward (goal, recipient), **por** looks back (reason) or at the way something is done.¶• Parts of the day: **por la mañana, por la tarde, por la noche**.¶• Fixed phrases: **por favor, por fin, por ejemplo, por aquí**.
A2|preps|Time prepositions: desde, desde hace, hasta, dentro de|53,54,3248,3249,3400,90,4078,4063,4066|Desde + point in time, desde hace + period; hasta = until; dentro de = in (future).|These prepositions place an action in time.¶T:Expression¦Use¦Example//**desde** + date¦since a point¦Me duele **desde** ayer.//**desde hace** + period¦for / for the last¦Estudio español **desde hace** un año.//**hasta** + time¦until, up to¦¡**Hasta** la semana que viene!//**dentro de** + period¦in (future)¦**Dentro de** una semana.//**hace** + period¦ago¦**Hace poco** lo vi.¶Estudio español **desde hace** un año. (For three days.)¶• Spanish uses the present tense for situations that continue: **Estudio... desde hace un año**, not he estudiado.¶• **Hace** + period before the verb means "ago": **Hace dos años viví allí.**¶• **Dentro de** is used for the future: **Dentro de una semana**; never use en for this meaning.

A2|conj|Cuando and mientras with the present|113,208,1006,2066,2124,4103,4108,3016,2896|Cuando = when, mientras = while; for habits or the present use the indicative, for future use the subjunctive.|**Cuando** (when) and **mientras** (while) introduce time clauses.¶• Habit or general: **Voy a nadar cuando hace calor**. A2|conj|Antes de and después de + infinitive|4104,4105,2125,2270,1036,1443,4121,4122,3257|Before and after a verb, Spanish uses antes de / después de + infinitive (not a full clause).|When the subject of both actions is the same, Spanish uses the preposition + **infinitive** instead of a full clause, where English can use "-ing".¶T:Structure¦meaning¦example//**antes de** + inf¦before (doing)¦**Antes de** irnos, tengo que ducharme. A2|conj|Que-clauses: creo que, dice que, me parece que|74,75,203,1298,3817,3882,3270,3671,3814|After creo que, pienso que, dice que, me parece que the verb is in the indicative; que is never omitted.|**Que** links an opinion, report or thought to what comes after it. A2|punct|Opening marks ¿ and ¡|46,47,48,51,2,24,25,27,32,80|Spanish questions and exclamations open with an upside-down mark and close with the normal mark.|In Spanish, questions and exclamations are marked at both ends: **¿...?** and **¡...!**. B1|tenses|Indefinido vs. imperfecto in a story|2896,3016,4108,3462,4111,4120,4121,3854,3855,4105|Imperfecto sets the scene or an ongoing state; indefinido gives the events that happen against it.|When you tell a story, think of two layers.¶• **Imperfecto** = background, description, what was going on: **Estaba cabreadísimo.** (I was furious.) **Cuando era pequeño, tenía un perro.** (When I was little, I had a dog.)¶• **Indefinido** = the events that move the story forward or interrupt the background: **Perdí los estribos.** (I lost my temper.) **Poco antes de medianoche llegó a casa.** (Shortly before midnight he came home.)¶Often one clause of each: **Ya estaba roto cuando lo compré.** (It was already broken when I bought it.) **No estaba en casa cuando vino el repartidor.** (I was not at home when the courier came.)¶The same verb can change meaning: **era** (was, state) / **fue** (was, a finished event): **La prueba fue desagradable, pero no era nada.** (The test was unpleasant, but it was nothing.) The meaning is the same.¶T:Before¦Attached//**¿Te puedo molestar un momento?**¦¿Puedo molestarte un momento?//**¿Me lo puedo probar?**¦¿Puedo probármelo?//**Me tengo que ir.**¦Tengo que irme.//**Lo estoy haciendo.**¦Estoy haciéndolo.¶Examples: **¿Puedes repetirlo, por favor?** (Can you repeat that?) **¿Puedo preguntarte una cosa?** (May I ask you something?) **¿Me lo puede enseñar en el mapa?** (Can you show me on the map?)¶Rules:¶• Never put the pronoun between the two verbs: wrong: **Puedo lo hacer**.¶• Attached pronouns often need a **written accent**: **probármelo**, **dándomelo**.¶• Negatives: **no** goes first, then the pronoun: **No me lo puedo permitir.** (I cannot afford it.) **No puedo permitírmelo.**¶• Reflexive verbs work the same: **Me tengo que ir.** = **Tengo que irme.**¶With the perfect tenses the pronoun always goes before **haber**: **Ya se lo he dicho.**
B1|order|Double object pronouns: me lo, se lo, te la|534,1841,637,898,213,2461,2844,2854,1405,159,270,275,2880|Indirect pronoun first, direct second (me lo, te la); le / les before lo / la / los / las becomes se.|When a sentence has both an indirect object (to whom) and a direct object (what), the order is fixed: **indirect + direct**, both before the verb or both attached to an infinitive.¶T:Indirect¦Direct¦Result//me¦lo¦**me lo**//te¦la¦**te la**//nos¦los¦**nos los**//le / les¦lo / la¦**se lo / se la**¶Examples: **Ya se lo he dicho.** (I have already told him.) **Esta te la debo.** (I owe you one.) **La fianza me la devuelven.** (They return the deposit to me.) **¿Me lo puede envolver para regalo?** (Can you gift-wrap it for me?)¶Important changes:¶• **le + lo → se lo** (never le lo): **Se lo paso al departamento correspondiente.** (I will forward it to the relevant department.) The se only shows it is third person, so add **a él / a ella / a usted** if unclear.¶• With imperatives and infinitives they attach in the same order: **Dímelo.** **No me lo puedo permitir** = **No puedo permitírmelo.**¶• **No te lo tomes a mal** (Do not take it badly) shows reflexive te + direct lo.¶English speakers often reverse the order. Remember: **me, te, se, nos** always come before **lo, la, los, las**.

B1|verbs|Affirmative imperative (tú, vosotros)|76,88,89,114,804,805,810,811,816,817,852,935,1009,2039,3286,4058|Tú imperative = third person present (habla, come); eight verbs are irregular: di, haz, ve, ten, pon, sal, ven, sé.|For **tú**, the affirmative imperative has the same form as the third person singular of the present: **hablar → habla**, **comer → come**, **abrir → abre**. Example: **Abre la ventana.** (Open the window.) **Cierra la puerta, por favor.** (Close the door, please.)¶Eight common verbs are irregular and short:¶T:Verb¦tú¦Verb¦tú//decir¦**di**¦salir¦**sal**//hacer¦**haz**¦venir¦**ven**//ir¦**ve**¦ser¦**sé**//tener¦**ten**¦poner¦**pon**¶Examples: **Pon la mesa, por favor.** (Set the table, please.) **¡Date prisa!** (Hurry up!)¶For **vosotros** (Spain), drop the final -r of the infinitive and add -d: **hablad**, **comed**, **abrid**, **venid**. In reflexive verbs the d disappears: **sentaos**, **callaos** (the only exception is **idos**). Latin America uses **ustedes** with the subjunctive form instead (**hablen**).¶Politeness: add **por favor**, or soften with a question (¿Puedes...?). The bare imperative is fine among friends and for instructions.
B1|verbs|Negative imperative: no hables, no vengas|174,224,1081,1421,3651,3683,1590,4190,270,159|For a negative command use no + the present subjunctive: no hables, no comas, no vengas.|Negative commands are not formed from the affirmative imperative. Use **no + present subjunctive**.¶T:Verb¦Affirmative¦Negative (tú)//hablar¦habla¦**no hables**//comer¦come¦**no comas**//venir¦ven¦**no vengas**//hacer¦haz¦**no hagas**//ser¦sé¦**no seas**//ir¦ve¦**no vayas**¶Examples: **No te preocupes.** (Do not worry.) **¡No tengas miedo!** (Do not be afraid!) **No te olvides de echarle sal al agua.** (Do not forget to salt the water.) **No dejes el grifo abierto tanto rato.** (Do not leave the tap running so long.)¶With pronouns, they stay **before** the verb in negative commands, but are attached in affirmative ones: **Cálmate** → **No te calmes.** **Díselo** → **No se lo digas.**¶The same rule works for **usted**: **No se preocupe.**, and for **vosotros**: **No os preocupéis.** (The affirmative vosotros form is not used negatively.)
B1|verbs|Imperative with pronouns: dímelo, siéntate, ponte|113,152,261,368,1439,3726,3851,4093,6073,935,811,3684,4058|In affirmative commands, pronouns attach to the verb (escríbeme, dímelo); add an accent to keep the stress.|In **affirmative** commands, object and reflexive pronouns are written **after the verb as one word**: **Escríbeme.** (Write to me.) **Avísame con tiempo.** (Let me know in good time.) **Ponte cómodo.** (Make yourself comfortable.) **Siéntate.** (Sit down.)¶The stress stays on the original syllable, so you often need a **written accent**: **dime → dímelo**, **escribe → escríbeme**, **pon → ponlo → póntelo**. Count back: if the word has the stress on the third syllable from the end, it needs an accent.¶Order with two pronouns: **indirect (me, te, le/se, nos) + direct (lo, la, los, las)**: **Pruébalo.** (Try it.) **Déjame terminar.** (Let me finish.) **Díselo.** (Tell it to him.) **Dámelo.** (Give it to me.) With reflexive verbs the final letter may change: **¡Tranquilízate!**, **¡Date prisa!** (from darse prisa).¶In **negative** commands the pronouns go before the verb and no accent is needed: **No te preocupes.**, **No me lo digas.**¶Tip: the same attaching rule applies to infinitives and gerunds (**ayudarme**, **dándome**).
B1|verbs|Verbs like gustar: encantar, molestar, apetecer, doler|108,124,142,448,892,1324,1325,1330,2111,2272,3693,3707,2064,2297|The thing liked is the subject; the person is an indirect pronoun: me gusta el café, me gustan los libros.|With **gustar** and similar verbs the thing that causes the feeling is the **subject**, and the person who feels it is expressed by an **indirect object pronoun** (**me, te, le, nos, os, les**). The verb agrees with the thing, not the person.¶T:Pronoun¦verb¦thing//**Me**¦gusta / encanta¦la película (singular)//**Te**¦gustan / encantan¦las películas (plural)//**Le**¦apetece¦algo dulce¶Common verbs: **encantar** (love), **molestar** (bother), **interesar**, **importar** (mind), **apetecer** (feel like), **doler** (hurt), **faltar** (be missing), **parecer** (seem), **dar igual** (not matter).¶Examples: **Me ha encantado la película.** (I loved the film.) **Me apetece algo dulce.** (I feel like something sweet.) **Me duele la rodilla.** (My knee hurts.) **¿Te importa si abro la ventana?** (Do you mind if I open the window?) **Le falta un poco de sal.** (It needs a little salt.)¶To name the person, add **a + noun** or **a mí / a ti / a él**: **A mi hermana le encanta bailar.** An infinitive counts as singular: **Me apetece salir.**¶Tip for English speakers: do not say "yo gusto". The person never becomes the subject.
B1|verbs|Acabar de, volver a, dejar de, seguir: aspect verbs|618,878,2488,2096,2565,3429,4404,5564,4253,1582|Acabar de + inf = just did; volver a + inf = do again; dejar de + inf = stop; seguir + gerund = keep on.|These short constructions add the idea of time or repetition to an action.¶T:Phrase¦Meaning¦Example//**acabar de + inf**¦to have just¦**Acabamos de llegar.** (We have just arrived.)//**volver a + inf**¦to do again¦**El tren vuelve a llegar tarde.** (The train is late again.)//**dejar de + inf**¦to stop¦**¡He dejado de fumar!** (I have quit smoking!)//**seguir + gerund**¦to keep doing¦**La brecha sigue aumentando.** (The gap keeps growing.)//**empezar a + inf**¦to begin¦**Los días empiezan a alargarse.** (The days are starting to get longer.)¶Notes:¶• **acabar de** is only used in the present or imperfect: **Me acabo de despertar.** (I have just woken up.) The past (**acabé de**) means "I finished".¶• **volver a** sometimes also means "get back to a state": **Vuelvo a estar en forma.** (I am back in shape.)¶• **No volvemos a ir nunca más.** (We are never going there again.)¶Remember the preposition: **a** or **de** is required before the infinitive, but never before a gerund.
B1|verbs|Se me olvidó: accidental events with se|118,139,1659,1809,4094,1833,2949,914,1308|Se + me / te / le + verb makes an event happen to someone: se me olvidó, se me ha roto, se me cae.|To say something happened unintentionally, Spanish makes the **thing** the subject and shows the person with an indirect pronoun. It sounds less blaming than **Olvidé** (I forgot) and shows that it was not on purpose. Add **a** + noun/pronoun for emphasis: **A mí se me olvidó.**
B1|verbs|Verbs with fixed prepositions: depender de, contar con|492,493,498,2913,3044,3731,4205,6065,6054,6390|Many Spanish verbs need a fixed preposition (depender de, contar con, fijarse en); learn them as a pair.|The preposition after a verb is often not the one you expect from English. B1|modal|Tener que vs. hay que: personal vs. impersonal obligation|110,111,145,159,169,243,846,850,897,913,1004,1065,1074,2509,4825,5883|Tener que + inf = someone must; hay que + inf = it is necessary (general, no subject).|Both mean "must / have to", but they differ in who is obliged.¶• **Tener que + infinitive** has a subject and is conjugated: **Tengo que llamar al casero.** (I have to call the landlord.) **Me tengo que ir.** (I have to go.) **Tenemos que seguir.** (We have to keep going.) **Tengo que confesarte algo.** (I have to confess something to you.)¶• **Hay que + infinitive** is impersonal and only has this one form (also **había que**, **habrá que**, **habría que**): **Hay que fregar el suelo.** (The floor needs mopping.) **Hay que aprender de la historia.** (We have to learn from history.) **Es algo que hay que ver sí o sí.** (That is a must-see.)¶Negatives differ:¶T:Form¦Meaning//**No tengo que ir**¦I do not have to go (not necessary)//**No hay que ir**¦One should not go (it is forbidden or unwise)//**No hay que creerse todo lo que pone en internet.**¦You should not believe everything online.¶Pronouns can go before **tener** or attach to the infinitive: **Me tengo que ir** = **Tengo que irme.**¶For strong necessity with no choice, **tener que** also expresses logical conclusion: **Eso tiene que quedar en familia.**
B1|modal|Poder: ability, permission and polite requests|49,50,55,85,95,115,127,213,216,258,151,231,233|Puedo / puedes + infinitive asks or gives permission; podría / podrías makes the request more polite.|**Poder** (o → ue: puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, podéis, pueden) covers ability, possibility and permission.¶• **Requests:** **¿Puedes repetirlo, por favor?** (Can you repeat that, please?) **¿Puedes ayudarme?** (Can you help me?)¶• **Asking permission:** **¿Puedo preguntarte una cosa?** (May I ask you something?) **¿Puedo tutearte?** (May I use tú with you?) **¿Puedo añadir algo rápido?** (May I quickly add something?)¶• **Giving permission:** **Puede tutearme, si quiere.** (You may use tú with me, if you like.)¶• **More polite with the conditional:** **¿Podrías hablar más despacio, por favor?** (Could you speak more slowly, please?) **¿Podría decirme dónde está la estación?** (Could you tell me where the station is?) **¿Me lo podrías deletrear?** (Could you spell it for me?)¶Use **podrías** with people you call tú and **podría** with usted. In the indicative, **No puedo** also refuses an invitation: **Hoy no puedo.** (I cannot today.)¶Do not confuse **poder** (can / be able to, circumstances) with **saber** (know how to, skill): **Sabe escuchar muy bien.** (He is a good listener.)
B1|modal|Deber and debería: obligation and advice|1317,1860,3882,4170,2476,4195,4182|Debo / debes + inf = duty; the conditional debería / deberíamos gives softer advice (should).|**Deber + infinitive** expresses duty or recommendation.¶• **Present** (debo, debes, debe, debemos, debéis, deben) is a stronger duty: **Debes descansar.** (You must rest.) It sounds firmer than **tener que** in some contexts.¶• **Conditional (debería, deberías, deberíamos)** is the normal way to give advice or make suggestions: **Deberíamos reservar antes.** (We should book in advance.) **Deberíamos sopesar el riesgo.** (We should weigh up the risk.) **Opino que deberíamos esperar.** (I think we should wait.) **Deberíamos hacer un calendario.** (We should make a schedule.) **¿Qué debería ir a ver?** (What should I go see?)¶• **Debería + haber + participle** = should have done: **Eso ya debería haberse hecho hace tiempo.** (That should have been done a long time ago.)¶Do not confuse with **deber de + infinitive**, which means probability: **Debe de estar en casa.** (He must be at home.)¶Compared with English, Spanish uses the plain conditional of deber where English says "should" or "ought to", and "have to" is usually **tener que** or **hay que**.
B1|modal|Soler + infinitive: usually, tend to|208,1355,3479,4408,4638,4802|Soler + infinitive says what usually happens; it exists only in the present and imperfect.|**Soler** (o → ue: suelo, sueles, suele, solemos, soléis, suelen) translates "usually" or "tend to". It works like a modal and always takes an infinitive.¶• **Habits:** **Solemos comer fuera.** (We usually eat out.) **¿Qué sueles hacer cuando no trabajas?** (What do you usually do when you are not working?)¶• **Typical results:** **Me suele doler la cabeza cuando estoy estresado.** (I often get headaches when I am stressed.) **El plástico suele acabar en el mar.** (Plastic often ends up in the sea.)¶• **General tendencies:** **En los pueblos, internet suele ir lento.** (In the countryside the internet is often slow.) **Las mujeres suelen ganar menos que los hombres.** (Women often earn less than men.)¶Tense: only the present (**suelo**) and imperfect (**solía**, for past habits: **Solía ir a pie.**). It has no future and rarely appears in the perfect.¶Compared with the adverb **normalmente**, soler keeps the sentence compact: **Suelo levantarme a las siete.** = **Normalmente me levanto a las siete.**¶Careful: the noun **el suelo** (floor) looks similar.
B1|articles|Days of the week: el sábado vs. los sábados|450,615,1811,2202,2225,3612,4052,4048,4050,4203,2041|Use el/la + weekday for one day and los + weekday for a habit; no preposition is needed (not on).|Spanish uses the definite article with days of the week, and the weekday itself needs no preposition for "on".¶• One specific day: **el** + weekday. B1|articles|El agua, un hambre: feminine nouns with stressed a|866,1206,1303,2086,1310,5369,1773,959|Feminine nouns starting with stressed a- take el/un in the singular but stay feminine: el agua fría.|Feminine nouns that begin with a stressed **a-** or **ha-** take **el** or **un** in the singular. B1|articles|No article after sin; medio and media|1224,1405,1427,870,2857,2045,1297,1417,2890|After sin, and with medio/media, Spanish drops the indefinite article: sin azúcar, medio kilo.|English often needs "a" or "an"; Spanish omits the indefinite article in several fixed patterns.¶• After **sin** (without) with a general noun: café **sin azúcar** (coffee without sugar), cerveza **sin alcohol**, **sin cebolla**, pagar **sin contacto**, quedarse **sin llaves**.¶• After **con** when the noun is not specific: una habitación **con baño**. B1|nouns|Tricky gender: el día, el mapa, la foto, el sofá|905,1605,1805,2461,2478,2628,1027,3299,4049|Some nouns break the -o masculine / -a feminine pattern: el día, el mapa, el sofá, la foto, la mano.|Most nouns ending in **-o** are masculine and most in **-a** feminine, but many common words do not follow this.¶T:Masculine in -a¦Feminine in -o¦Masculine, other ending//el día (the day)¦la mano (the hand)¦el sofá (the sofa)//el mapa (the map)¦la foto (the photo)¦el análisis (the test)//el problema, el tema, el idioma¦la moto (the motorbike)¦el lavavajillas¶• Me he pasado todo **el día** limpiando. B1|nouns|Plural spelling: -z to -ces, -ión to -iones, invariable nouns|468,482,2018,2081,2201,3257,1319,828,856,449|Add -s after a vowel and -es after a consonant; z becomes c, and the accent on -ión disappears.|The basic rules for plural nouns, plus the spelling changes B1 learners need.¶• Ends in a vowel: add **-s**. casa, casas; tarde, tardes.¶• Ends in a consonant: add **-es**. ciudad, ciudad**es**; mujer, mujer**es**.¶• Ends in **-z**: change to **-ces**. vez, **veces**; luz, **luces**. Tres **veces** por semana. (Three times a week.)¶• Words in **-ión** lose the written accent: la ración, las **raciones**; la habitación, las **habitaciones**. The stress stays on the same syllable.¶• Words that end in an unstressed -s do not change; only the article shows the plural: el lavavajillas, **los** lavavajillas; el cumpleaños, **los** cumpleaños; el análisis, **los** análisis.¶• Stressed vowel + s: add -es (el país, los países; el inglés, los ingleses; el autobús, los autobuses).¶**Mixed groups:** use the masculine plural: los padres (parents or fathers), los hermanos (brothers and sisters).
B1|nouns|Nouns that are only (or usually) plural|121,1633,1672,3310,922,512,1820,4222,2481|Words like vacaciones, gafas and gracias are plural in Spanish: Estoy de vacaciones.|Some nouns are normally plural in Spanish, even when English uses a singular word.¶• **Las vacaciones** (vacation, holidays): Estoy **de vacaciones**. (I'm on vacation.) ¿Cuántos días **de vacaciones** tienes? (How many vacation days do you have?)¶• **Las gafas** (glasses), **los pantalones** (trousers), **las tijeras** (scissors), **los vaqueros** (jeans): No encuentro **mis gafas**. (I can't find my glasses.)¶• **Las gracias** (thanks) with dar: Quería darte **las gracias**. (I wanted to thank you.)¶• **Las ganas, los celos, los ahorros**: tener ganas de + infinitive (to feel like doing).¶**Mistakes to avoid:**¶• Vacación is not used for a holiday period; say vacaciones, even for a short break (un día de vacaciones).¶• To say "a pair of glasses" or "a pair of trousers", use the plural article and verb: Mis gafas **están** rotas.¶• Gracias itself never changes: muchas gracias, mil gracias.
B1|pronouns|Two object pronouns together: me lo, se lo|534,2910,1405,2461,2854,2844,2880,2905,3304,1710|Indirect pronoun first, then direct (me lo, te la); le/les becomes se before lo/la/los/las.|When a sentence has both an indirect object (to/for someone) and a direct object (the thing), the two pronouns stand together before the verb, always in this order: **indirect + direct**.¶T:Pattern¦Example¦Meaning//me + lo¦**Me lo** llevo.¦I'll take it.//te + lo¦**Te lo** puedo explicar.¦I can explain it to you.//se + lo¦Ya **se lo** he dicho.¦I've already told him/her.//nos + la¦**Nos la** han enviado.¦They sent it to us.¶• **le / les + lo/la/los/las becomes se**: never say le lo. El paquete **se lo** dejaron al vecino. (They left the package with the neighbor.)¶• The pair can never be split by other words; no is placed before them: **No me lo** puedo permitir. (I can't afford that.)¶• Because se can mean to him, her, you (usted) or them, add a clarifying phrase if needed: Se lo dije **a Ana**.¶**Tip:** remember "indirect before direct", and that me/te/nos/se always come before lo/la/los/las.
B1|pronouns|Where to put the pronoun: before the verb or attached|50,55,61,85,94,95,107,127,2844,2866,2880,2905,935|Pronouns go before a conjugated verb but attach to infinitives, gerunds and positive commands.|Object and reflexive pronouns (me, te, lo, la, le, se, nos, les) change position depending on the verb form.¶• **Before a conjugated verb** (and in negative commands): **Lo** he pedido por internet. (I ordered it online.) **No lo** hagas. (Don't do it.)¶• **Attached to the end** of an infinitive, a gerund or a positive command: ¿Puedes ayudar**me**? (Can you help me?) Quería pregunta**rte** algo. (I wanted to ask you something.) Pon**te** cómodo. (Make yourself comfortable.)¶• With a verb + infinitive you can choose: ¿**Me lo** puedo probar? or ¿Puedo probár**melo**? (Can I try it on?) **Lo** voy a devolver = Voy a devolver**lo**. (I'm going to return it.)¶• Attaching a pronoun can create a written accent so that the stress stays: decir**me** (no accent), explíca**melo**, dí**melo**.¶**Tip:** with two verbs in a row you can place the pronouns before the first or after the infinitive, never between the two verbs.
B1|pronouns|Direct object pronouns: lo, la, los, las|91,497,1257,1697,2804,2805,2864,2866,2896,2904|Lo/la/los/las replace the thing or person; lo also stands for ideas and masculine people in Spain.|A direct object pronoun replaces a noun that answers "what?" or "whom?" and agrees with it in gender and number.¶T:Singular¦Plural//masculine: **lo**¦**los**//feminine: **la**¦**las**¶• ¿Tiene el vestido en azul? **Lo** tiene. → ¿**Lo** tiene en azul? (I didn't order this.) The noun is repeated by the pronoun.¶**Spain note (leísmo):** for a male person, many Spaniards use **le** instead of lo: **Le** veo mañana. B1|pronouns|Indirect objects: le, les and a + noun|527,225,82,472,2910,930,534,1710|Le/les is often used even when the person is named: Les he leído un cuento a los niños.|The indirect object pronoun tells who receives or benefits from the action: **me, te, le, nos, os, les**.¶• Spanish normally repeats the person: the pronoun is there **and** the full noun with **a**. **Les** he leído un cuento **a los niños**. (I read the children a story.)¶• Dale **a tu madre** un beso de mi parte. (Give your mother my love.)¶• **Le envío** una convocatoria. (I'm sending you an invitation.) B1|pronouns|After prepositions: mí, ti, conmigo, contigo|223,3678,3694,3802,3812,610,3723,4124,4213,210|After a preposition use mí, ti, él...; but con + mí/ti = conmigo/contigo, and sin mí is fine.|After most prepositions Spanish uses special "prepositional" pronouns.¶T:Subject¦After preposition¦With con//yo¦**mí**¦**conmigo**//tú¦**ti**¦**contigo**//él / ella / usted¦él / ella / usted¦con él / con ella//nosotros, vosotros, ellos¦(same)¦con nosotros ...¶• Es como un hermano para **mí**. B1|pronouns|Verbs like gustar: encantar, apetecer, doler, importar|108,448,485,892,925,932,1320,1324,1301,2064,3697|With gustar-type verbs the thing liked is the subject; the person is the indirect object: Me gustan los libros.|Gustar does not mean "to like" word for word; it means "to be pleasing to". B1|pronouns|Indefinites and double negatives: algo, nada, alguien, nadie|109,26,87,151,219,243,518,568,916,941,955,1291,1324,2495,4117|Algo/alguien/algún are positive; nada/nadie/ningún are negative and need no before the verb.|Indefinite pronouns come in positive and negative pairs.¶T:Positive¦Negative//algo (something)¦nada (nothing)//alguien (someone)¦nadie (no one)//algún, alguna (some)¦ningún, ninguna (no, not any)¶• ¿Puedo añadir **algo** rápido? (I'm looking for someone to take over my flat.)¶• **Algún** and **ningún** are the forms before a masculine singular noun: ¿Tienes **algún** plan? (Do you have any plans?) **Algún** día iré a Japón. (Someday I'll go to Japan.)¶• Spanish uses **double negatives**: if the negative word comes after the verb, put **no** before it. **No** pasa **nada**. (No problem.) El casero **no** se ocupa **de nada**. (The landlord doesn't take care of anything.) **No** se deja decir **nada** por **nadie**.¶• If the negative word comes first, no is dropped: **Nadie** lo sabe. **Nada** me gusta.¶**Tip:** alguien and nadie take the personal a when they are the object: No veo **a nadie**; Busco **a alguien**.
B1|pronouns|Neuter pronouns: esto, eso, aquello|40,48,70,83,92,101,102,117,122,906,923,1225|Esto, eso and aquello point to something unnamed or to a whole idea; they never take an accent.|The neuter demonstratives **esto, eso, aquello** refer to something you cannot name, an unknown object or a whole situation. (This looks like a battlefield.)¶• **eso** = that (near you, or an idea just mentioned): ¿Qué quieres decir con **eso**? (What do you mean by that?) **Eso** depende. (That depends.) Me alegra oír **eso**. (I'm glad to hear that.)¶• **aquello** = that over there / long ago and far away: **Aquello** fue una época difícil. (That was a hard time.)¶**Spelling:** the masculine and feminine forms éste, ése used to carry an accent, but esto/eso/aquello never did; today the accent is no longer needed on any demonstrative.¶**Tip:** if you can point to a noun, use este/ese/aquel with its gender (este libro, esa mesa). Use the neuter forms only when you have no noun: ¿Qué es eso?
B1|pronouns|Lo que: what, the thing that|124,1301,1323,1299,1403,281,1062,2942,237|Lo que means what / the thing(s) that; it links a clause and does not change for gender or number.|**Lo que** introduces a clause and means "what" or "the thing(s) that". B1|adjectives|Absolute superlative with -ísimo|1247,1260,1419,2105,3290,3803,3827,1345|Add -ísimo/a to the adjective to say very, extremely: rico, riquísimo; fácil, facilísimo.|The ending **-ísimo / -ísima / -ísimos / -ísimas** means "extremely" and replaces muy + adjective.¶• Drop the final vowel and add the ending: bueno → **buenísimo**, lleno → **llenísimo**, claro → **clarísimo**. ¡Esto está **buenísimo**! B1|adjectives|Equality and sameness: tan, tanto, igual de, lo mismo|516,1265,1403,2935,3695,3816|Use tan + adjective/adverb + como, tanto + noun + como, and lo mismo que for equality.|To say two things are equal, Spanish uses a family of **tan / tanto ... como** structures.¶• **tan** + adjective or adverb: no estoy **tan** seguro de eso. B1|preps|Por: reason, place, means and exchange|452,465,487,535,612,628,205,207,1283,502,603|Por answers why (cause), through where, by what means, and for how long; it is the thanks/worry/exchange preposition.|**Por** looks backwards at the cause, or moves through a space. B1|preps|Desde, hasta, hacia: points in space and time|53,491,1623,1717,2121,2212,2623,4202,35,36|Desde marks the starting point, hasta the end; hacia gives a direction. B1|conj|Time clauses: cuando, mientras, cada vez que, desde que|4103,1006,4104,4105,4106,4108,4109,2896,3016,689,2124,2274|Time conjunctions link two actions: cuando (when), mientras (while), antes de / después de + infinitive.|Time clauses place one action relative to another. B1|conj|Reasons and results: porque, por eso, así que, ya que|4247,2758,250,6058,6385,6057,6059,6060|Porque / ya que give the reason; por eso, así que and por esta razón give the result.|Use different words depending on whether you give the **cause** or the **consequence**.¶T:Role¦Words¦Example//cause¦**porque**, **ya que**, **puesto que**, **como**¦**Llego tarde porque no ha venido el autobús.** (I am late because the bus did not come.)//cause (known)¦**ya que**¦**Ya que estamos: ¿tienes mi llave?** (While we are at it: do you have my key?)//result¦**por eso**, **por esta razón**, **así que**¦**Por eso propongo que esperemos.** (That is why I suggest we wait.)//result (informal)¦**así que**¦**Solo se vive una vez, ¡así que adelante!** (You only live once, so go for it!)¶Details:¶• **Porque** (one word, no accent) answers **¿Por qué?** (why?). Do not mix it with **por qué** (two words, question), **porqué** (the reason) and **por que**.¶• Use **como** at the start of the sentence for a cause that is already known: **Como no ha venido el autobús, llego tarde.**¶• **Eso se debe a que** introduces an explanation: **Eso se debe a que nadie tiene tiempo.** (That is because nobody has time.) **Eso hace que muchos se rindan.** (That makes many give up.)¶With a cause that is denied or hypothetical, the subjunctive is used: **No porque sea caro, es malo.**
B1|conj|Contrast: pero, sin embargo, en cambio, aunque|111,159,286,537,653,6061,6127,6122,6046,6071,6130,983|Pero for a simple contrast; sin embargo / en cambio for a sharper contrast; aunque for a concession.|Spanish expresses contrast with a graded set of words.¶• **pero** (but) is the everyday word: **Me saca de quicio, pero lo quiero.** (He drives me mad, but I love him.) **Lo siento, pero ahora me tengo que ir.** (Sorry, but I have to go now.)¶• **sin embargo** and **no obstante** (however) are used in writing and formal speech, usually after a full stop: **Sin embargo, hay que matizar que existen excepciones.** (However, one has to add that there are exceptions.)¶• **en cambio** (on the other hand) contrasts two things or people: **En cambio, la segunda opción es más barata.** (In contrast, the second option is cheaper.)¶• **por un lado... por otro (lado)**: **Por un lado es caro, pero por otro se ahorra tiempo.** (On the one hand it is expensive, but on the other you save time.)¶• **aunque** (although): **Aunque las cifras pintan bien, sigo siendo prudente.** (Although the figures look good, I remain cautious.) With the indicative it concedes a known fact; with the subjunctive it means "even if".¶• **Le he perdonado, pero no lo he olvidado.** (I have forgiven him, but not forgotten.)¶Tip: **pero** needs a comma before it; **sino** is used instead after a negative to correct it: **No es caro, sino barato.** (It is not expensive but cheap.)

B1|conj|Relative clauses: lo que, algo que, nada que|124,237,281,1062,1301,1323,3027,3755,4168,4601,109,2521,3837,955|Que links a noun and a description; lo que means "what" and refers to a general idea.|**Que** is the most common relative pronoun: it refers to people, things or ideas and never changes. **Lo que** means "what / the thing that".¶• **Lo que** (what): **Solo compro lo que de verdad necesito.** (I only buy what I really need.) **Uno hace lo que puede.** (You do what you can.) **Me da igual lo que hagamos.** (I do not care what we do.) **Lo que más me gusta cocinar es comida italiana.** (What I like cooking most is Italian food.)¶• **algo / nada / alguien que**: **No hay nada que agradecer.** (There is nothing to thank for.) **¿Tiene algo que declarar?** (Do you have anything to declare?) **Aquí hay algo que no cuadra.** (Something does not add up here.)¶• **Busco a alguien que se quede con mi piso.** (I am looking for someone to take over my flat.) The person is not yet known, so the subjunctive follows.¶• After **todo** use **todo lo que**: **No hay que creerse todo lo que pone en internet.**¶Tips:¶• English drops "that" (the film I saw); Spanish **never** drops que.¶• After a preposition use **el que / la que / donde / quien** instead: **la casa en la que vivo**, **la gente con quien trabajo**.¶• Do not confuse **que** (relative) with **qué** (question).
B1|conj|Si-clauses: real conditions with si + present|136,3006,233,264,314,318,3189,6119|Si + present indicative expresses a real possibility; the main clause uses present, future or imperative.|A conditional sentence has an **if-part** (si + verb) and a **result**. B1|neg|Question words with prepositions: de qué, desde cuándo|53,92,93,153,204,205,206,255,280,1323|The preposition goes first and stays with the question word: ¿De qué...?, ¿A dónde...?, ¿Con quién...?|In Spanish the preposition always stands **in front of** the question word; it cannot be left at the end, as in English "Who are you talking to?".¶T:English¦Spanish//What do you know her from?¦**¿De qué la conoces?** (¿De qué conoces a Lisa?)//How long...?¦**¿Desde cuándo...?** / **¿Cuánto tiempo llevas...?**//What are you getting at?¦**¿Adónde quieres llegar?**//What for?¦**¿Para qué...?**//With whom?¦**¿Con quién...?**¶Examples: **¿Desde cuándo estudias español?** (How long have you been studying Spanish?) **¿De qué conoces a Lisa, por cierto?** (How do you actually know Lisa?) **¿En qué sentido lo dices?** (In what sense do you say that?) **¿Cuánto tiempo llevas en la ciudad?** (How long have you been in the city?) **¿Qué quieres decir con eso?** (What do you mean by that?)¶Useful details:¶• **Qué** is invariable; **cuál / cuáles** (which) and **quién / quiénes** (who) agree in number.¶• **Cuánto, cuánta, cuántos, cuántas** agree with the noun: **¿Cuánta gente viene?**¶• All question words carry a written accent: **qué, cómo, cuándo, dónde, quién, cuál, cuánto**.¶• Tip: **¿Cómo?** means "pardon?" as well as "how?".
B1|mood|Present subjunctive: forms and regular patterns|212,3681,3697,3700,3808,3813,3814,113,1080,4102,4236,294,3696,3809|Take the yo form of the present, drop -o and add the opposite vowel: hablo → hable, como → coma.|The present subjunctive is formed from the **first person singular of the present indicative**: remove **-o** and add the "opposite" endings.¶T:Verb type¦Endings¦Example//-ar¦-e, -es, -e, -emos, -éis, -en¦**hable, hables**//-er / -ir¦-a, -as, -a, -amos, -áis, -an¦**coma, viva, salga**¶Irregular yo forms carry over: **tengo → tenga**, **hago → haga**, **salgo → salga**, **vengo → venga**, **pongo → ponga**, **digo → diga**, **conozco → conozca**. Stem-changing verbs keep their change in the stressed forms (**pueda**, **quiera**) and -ir verbs also change in nosotros (**durmamos**).¶Six irregulars not based on yo: **ser → sea**, **ir → vaya**, **estar → esté**, **saber → sepa**, **dar → dé**, **haber → haya**.¶Examples: **Espero que estés bien.** (I hope you are well.) **Me alegro de que todo haya salido bien.** (I am glad everything went well.) **Escríbeme cuando tengas tiempo.** (Write to me when you have time.) **Es una pena que no vengas.** (It is a shame you are not coming.)¶The perfect subjunctive is **haya + participle**: **Me parece genial que hayas venido.**

B1|numbers|Dates and months in Spanish|1827,4011,439,4041,1716,1808,4119,1717|Say el + number + de + month: el uno de octubre; in + month needs en; a partir de means "from".|Spanish gives dates as **el + cardinal number + de + month**. Months are written with a lowercase letter.¶• Hoy es **uno de mayo**. (Today is the first of May.) Empiezo **el uno de octubre**. (I start on October first.)¶• Only the first of the month uses **uno** (or primero); other days use ordinary numbers: el **dos** de mayo, el **veinte** de junio.¶• With the month alone use **en**: Mi cumpleaños es **en** junio. (My birthday is in June.) Estaré disponible **a partir del** lunes. (I'll be reachable again from Monday.)¶• Full date with the year: el 12 de marzo **de** 2026 (de before the year too).¶• Other date phrases: **antes del** viernes (before/by Friday), **a partir de** (from...on), **hasta el** viernes (until Friday), **a mediados de** mes, **a finales de** mes.¶**Tip:** the abbreviation order is day/month/year (12/3/2026 = 12 March), unlike in the US. Note the article **el** before the number, and **no** preposition before the day: Nos vemos **el** 14.
B1|numbers|Time spans: hace, dentro de, llevar and desde hace|54,2212,607,4215,1297,2606,4116,2492,491,1429|Hace + time = ago; dentro de + time = in; llevar + time + gerund = for; desde hace = for/since.|Spanish has several short structures for how much time has passed or will pass.¶• **hace + time** (ago): **Hace** un rato ha llamado alguien. B1|particles|Tag questions: ¿verdad?, ¿no?|116,148,202,277|Add ¿verdad? or ¿no? at the end of a statement to check or confirm, like "right?" or "isn't it?".|Spanish has no complicated tag-question system like English ("isn't it", "don't you").
