B1|punct|Question and exclamation marks: ¿ ¡|121,216,204,219,62,210,487,3629,3687,1274|Open with ¿ or ¡ at the start of the question or exclamation, even if it is mid-sentence.|Spanish uses an **opening mark** (¿ ¡) as well as a closing one (? !). The opening mark is placed where the question or exclamation actually starts, not necessarily at the start of the sentence.¶• ¿Qué haces aquí? ¡Qué bien!¶• If something comes before the question, begin the mark later: Hablando de vacaciones, **¿**adónde vas? (Speaking of vacation, where are you going?) Oye, **¿**tienes algún plan para hoy? (Say, do you have any plans today?)¶• The same for exclamations: ¡Cuánto tiempo sin verte! (Long time no see!) ¡Qué detalle por tu parte! (That's so sweet of you!)¶• Do not repeat the marks in correct writing (not ¿¿¿Qué???); for a question that is also an exclamation you can combine them: ¡¿Qué?!¶• Never put a full stop after ? or !. The next sentence starts with a capital letter.¶**Tip:** a missing opening ¿ or ¡ is one of the most typical spelling mistakes of English speakers writing Spanish, and it is marked as wrong in exams such as the DELE.
B1|punct|Accents on question words and por qué vs. porque|1820,2603,3007,4201,493,3644,3699,93,204,62,210|Question and exclamation words carry an accent (qué, cómo, dónde); the same words without an accent link clauses.|The words **qué, quién, cuál, cuándo, cuánto, cómo, dónde, adónde, por qué** take a written accent when they ask a question or exclaim, in direct or indirect form.¶• Direct: ¿**Cuántos** días de vacaciones tienes? ¿**Dónde** se factura el equipaje? ¿**Cuándo** tienes tiempo esta semana?¶• Indirect: No entiendo **por qué** lo hizo. B1|punct|Written accents: agudas, llanas, esdrújulas|95,465,837,526,1201,1027,1252,18,450,840|Stress falls on the last, second-to-last or third-to-last syllable; the tilde marks exceptions to the default.|The **default** stress is automatic, and a written accent (tilde) shows only the exceptions.¶• Words ending in **a vowel, n or s** are stressed on the **second-to-last** syllable: **ca**sa, **ha**blan, **lu**nes. B1|punct|Commas: introductory phrases, vocatives and before pero|3815,120,603,121,1714,4107,111,219,204|Use a comma after an introductory word or clause, around "por cierto", and before pero.|Spanish commas follow rules similar to English, with a few typical places to remember.¶• **After an introductory word or phrase:** En mi opinión**,** tienes razón. B1|style|Reported speech: dice que, me ha dicho que, dijo que|662,1671,3270,3952,2367,1585|Report what someone said with decir que + clause; tenses back-shift only after a past verb of saying.|To report speech use a verb of saying plus **que** (no comma or quotation marks needed).¶• **Present reporting verb (dice que):** the tenses stay the same: **El médico dice que tengo que descansar.** (The doctor says I have to rest.) **Mi intuición me dice que aquí hay gato encerrado.** (My gut tells me something is fishy.)¶• **Perfect reporting verb (ha dicho que):** **¡Ha dicho que sí!** (She said yes!) **He llamado para decir que estoy enfermo.** (I called to say I am ill.)¶• **Past reporting verb (dijo que...):** tenses usually shift back: present → imperfect, perfect → pluperfect, future → conditional: **Dijo que estaba cansado.** (He said he was tired.) **Dijo que vendría.** (He said he would come.)¶• **Other options:** **dicen que, se dice que, según** for unnamed sources: **Dicen que dijo Churchill...** (They say Churchill said...)¶Questions are reported with **si** or a question word: **Me preguntó si tenía tiempo.** (He asked me if I had time.)¶Changes of place and time: **hoy → ese día**, **mañana → al día siguiente**, **aquí → allí**.¶Tip: **decir** + imperative becomes **decir que + subjunctive**: **Dime que vengas** → **Me dijo que viniera.**

B2|tenses|Futuro simple: predictions and guesses|5017,4881,4172,4329,6268,164,6380,6347|Besides plans and predictions, the future can express a guess about the present: Serán las diez.|The **futuro simple** (infinitive + é, ás, á, emos, éis, án) covers three jobs.¶• Predictions and facts about the future: **Habrá** nuevas elecciones. B2|tenses|Condicional: politeness, advice and hypotheses|96,228,1694,5872,6156,6157,6347,6348,2476|The conditional (-ía) softens requests and states what would happen under some condition.|The **condicional simple** uses the infinitive plus the endings -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían (same irregular stems as the future: tendría, podría, sería, habría).¶• Politeness and softening: **Tendría** una pregunta. (The prescription must be used within 28 days.)¶• The pronoun attaches to the infinitive or comes before the conjugated verb: Eso **lo** tiene que decidir el jefe / Eso tiene que decidir**lo** el jefe.¶• It sounds natural when the information is already known or contrasted.¶Common mistake: leaving the pronoun out (La receta hay que usar) is wrong. The English equivalent is passive: The recipe must be used. This is a typical Spanish way to avoid the passive.

(I forgot the appointment; literally 'the appointment forgot itself on me'.)¶• Se **nos** ha averiado el coche. (Our car has broken down.)¶• Se **le** cayó el vaso. (The money slipped through my fingers.)¶The verb agrees with the thing that happened, not with the person: Se me olvidaron las llaves (plural), Se me olvidó la llave.¶Typical verbs: **olvidarse, caerse, romperse, perderse, acabarse, ocurrirse, quedarse**.¶• Add **a mí / a ti / a Juan** to stress the person: A Juan se le olvidó.¶• Compare with the personal version: **Olvidé** la cita (I forgot it, neutral) versus **Se me olvidó** (it slipped my mind, not my fault).¶Tip: do not say Yo olvidé mis llaves when you want to say it was an accident.
B2|pronouns|Prepositional pronouns: mí, ti, conmigo, contigo|267,570,708,1131,3678,3772,3802,3923,4124,5178,210,576|After a preposition use mí/ti/él (accent on mí); with con use conmigo/contigo; yo/tú after entre and según.|After most prepositions Spanish uses special pronouns:¶T:Subject¦After a preposition¦With con//yo¦mí¦conmigo//tú¦ti¦contigo//él / ella¦él / ella¦con él / con ella//nosotros¦nosotros¦con nosotros¶• Mí has a written accent to differ from the possessive mi: **para mí** (for me) vs. **mi** casa (my house). Ti never has an accent.¶• With **con**: **conmigo**, **contigo**, and **consigo** (with himself/herself).¶• After **entre**, **según**, **excepto**, **salvo**, **incluso** use yo and tú: **Entre tú y yo**... (Between you and me), **Según tú**, no es posible. (According to you, it is not possible.)¶• For emphasis or contrast, repeat the pronoun: **A mí** me gusta, pero a ti no. (I like it, but you don't.)¶• Reflexive after prepositions: **conmigo mismo**.¶Example: Estoy enfadado **contigo**. (I'm angry with you.)
B2|pronouns|Impersonal se: se puede, se dice, se habla de|192,759,4183,4549,4561,5329,4875,2132|se + 3rd person verb = a general 'one/you/people', or a passive with a thing as subject.|**Se** + a verb in the third person can express a general subject ('one', 'you', 'people') or a passive sense when a thing is the subject:¶• ¿**Se puede** entrar? / Eso **no se puede** negar. (There's no denying that.)¶• **Se habla** más abiertamente de la salud mental. (People talk more openly about mental health.)¶• With a plural thing, the verb agrees (pasiva refleja): **Se venden** pisos. (Flats are for sale.) El torneo **se celebra** en verano. (The tournament takes place in summer.)¶• With people as direct object, impersonal se uses the singular and a personal a: **Se aprecia a** los profesores. (Teachers are valued.)¶• The English 'you/they/one' always becomes se: No **se puede** meter a todos en el mismo saco. (You can't lump everyone together.)¶Common mistake: translating 'They say' as Ellos dicen. Use **Se dice que**... or Dicen que...¶Tip: do not confuse it with reflexive se (se lava) or the replacement se (se lo di).
B2|pronouns|Relative pronouns: quien, donde, el que, la que|1785,2791,2999,4191,4448,4962,1161,1128,1183,2309,6020|quien (people, 'the one who'), donde (place), el que / la que after prepositions (la libertad de la que).|Besides **que**, Spanish uses:¶• **quien / quienes** (people only; singular or plural): **Quien** viaja tiene mucho que contar. (Anyone who travels has stories to tell.) After a preposition: A **quien** madruga, Dios le ayuda. (God helps those who rise early.)¶• **el que / la que / los que / las que** replace que after prepositions and clarify who: La libertad **de la que** disfrutamos. (The freedom we enjoy.) Un golazo **de los que** hacen historia. (A goal of the kind that makes history.)¶• **donde** (place): Mi hogar está **donde** está mi familia. (Home is where my family is.) En casa es **donde** mejor desconecto.¶• **cuyo / cuya** (whose) agrees with the noun that follows, not the owner: La mujer **cuyo** hijo vino. (The woman whose son came.)¶Rules of thumb:¶• Que cannot follow a preposition for people: la chica con **la que** hablo, not con que.¶• **Quien** stands alone only in generalizations and proverbs.¶Tip: in everyday speech, **donde** can replace en el que for places.
B2|pronouns|Indefinite pronouns: alguien, nadie, cualquiera, cualquier|337,568,731,759,955,1335,1714,1985,1988,2735,2779,3567,3999|alguien / nadie for people, algo / nada for things; cualquier + noun drops -a; cualquiera stands alone.|• **alguien** (someone) and **nadie** (no one) are invariable and refer to people. **algo** and **nada** refer to things.¶• **Nadie** needs no before the verb when it follows it: No quiero contagiar a **nadie**. Nadie es imprescindible. (Nobody is irreplaceable.)¶• Direct object persons need a personal a: ¿Esperas **a alguien**? (Are you waiting for someone?)¶• **cualquier** (before a noun, masc. or fem.) = any: Para **cualquier** duda, quedo a su disposición. (For any questions, I'm at your disposal.) Puedo trabajar desde **cualquier** sitio. (I can work from anywhere.)¶• **cualquiera** (after the noun or alone) = anyone, whichever: Eso lo sabe **cualquiera**. (Anyone knows that.) Plural: cualesquiera, rare.¶• **alguno / ninguno** shorten to **algún / ningún** before masculine singular nouns: algún problema, ningún problema.¶• With a subjunctive clause: Busco a **alguien que** se quede con mi piso. (I'm looking for someone to take over my flat.)¶Tip: cualquier cosa = anything; cualquier persona = anyone.
B2|pronouns|Stressed possessives: culpa mía, un amigo suyo, lo mío|157,181,489,1786,276,1336|Long possessives (mío, tuyo, suyo) follow the noun or ser: es culpa mía, soy amigo suyo, no es lo mío.|There are two sets of possessives. The short ones (**mi, tu, su**) go before a noun. The long ones go after a noun or after ser, and agree in gender and number:¶T:mine¦yours¦his/hers/yours (formal)¦ours¦yours (vosotros)//mío, mía, míos, mías¦tuyo, tuya¦suyo, suya¦nuestro, nuestra¦vuestro, vuestra¶• After a noun, for emphasis or 'of mine': Fue culpa **mía**. (It was my fault.) Eso no es asunto **mío**. (That's none of my business.) Soy amigo **suyo**. (I'm a friend of hers.) ¡Madre **mía**! (My goodness!)¶• With the neuter **lo**: **lo mío** (my thing); No es **lo mío**. (It's not my thing.)¶• With the article, it replaces a noun: Mi coche y **el tuyo**. (My car and yours.) Never say un amigo de mí.¶• Not used with body parts or clothes in Spanish: Me lavo **las** manos (not mis manos).¶Tip: suyo can mean his, her, their or your (formal), so clarify with **de él, de ella, de ellos, de usted** if unclear.
B2|adjectives|Adjective position: un gran hombre vs. un hombre grande|681,723,780,789,1187,1396,1857,2248,3716,3717,201,576,1097,1667|Before the noun an adjective is subjective or figurative (gran, viejo); after it, it is literal and distinguishing.|Usually the adjective follows the noun and distinguishes it: un edificio **antiguo** (an old building). (She has a big heart.) Tengo un **buen** presentimiento. (I have a good feeling.)¶• After ser, the adjective is not shortened: Soy **nuevo** aquí. (I'm new here.)¶Tip: if in doubt, put the adjective after the noun.
B2|adjectives|Absolute superlative with -ísimo: carísimo, buenísimo|334,545,1033,1092,1247,1260,1345,1389,1419,2105,2243,2692,3125,3290|-ísimo (+ gender and number) means 'extremely ___': caro → carísimo, fácil → facilísimo.|The suffix **-ísimo, -ísima, -ísimos, -ísimas** makes an adjective extreme. It agrees with the noun it describes and is very common in speech.¶• Drop the final vowel: **bueno → buenísimo**, **caro → carísimo**, **llena → llenísima**. Esto está **buenísimo**. (This is delicious.)¶• Spelling changes keep the sound: **rico → riquísimo** (c → qu), **largo → larguísimo** (g → gu), **feliz → felicísimo** (z → c), **amable → amabilísimo** (-ble → -bil-).¶• Also: antiguo → antiquísimo, fácil → facilísimo.¶• The same ending exists on adverbs and quantity words: **muchísimo**, **muchísimas** deudas, **cerquísima**. Me duele **muchísimo**. (It hurts a lot.)¶• Some irregular forms: **bueno → óptimo**, **malo → pésimo**, **grande → máximo**, but buenísimo is more usual in conversation.¶• Do not combine with muy: not muy carísimo.¶Tip: it is stronger than muy + adjective.
B2|adjectives|Comparison: más que, tan como, cada vez más|1149,2923,4401,4403,4408,4438,2360,4574,2297,1819,4539,1386|más/menos + adj. + que; tan + adj. + como; cada vez más = increasingly; mayor/mejor are irregular.|• **más / menos + adjective + que**: Gano **más que** antes. Cada vez más personas viven solas.¶• Irregular: **bueno → mejor**, **malo → peor**, **grande → mayor** (older, bigger in abstract sense), **pequeño → menor**, **mucho → más**. B2|preps|Prepositional phrases: tras, ante, según, hacia, en vez de|3514,4390,5490,6339,4268,2702,4000,3148,4955,4600,6124,6106,5805,5875,2336|Formal prepositions: tras (after), ante (before/faced with), según, hacia, pese a, en cuanto a, a través de.|B2 texts use more precise prepositions and phrases:¶• **durante** (during, for a time): Alemania estuvo dividida **durante** más de cuarenta años. (About what time?)¶• **en vez de / en lugar de** + noun or infinitive: Reparar **en lugar de** tirar. B2|preps|Por vs. para: reasons, purposes, recipients and opinions|172,245,266,486,570,610,663,794,1370,1843,3699,5178,3799,2475|para = purpose, goal, recipient, deadline, opinion; por = cause, exchange, means, through, on behalf of.|**Para** looks forward (aim):¶• Purpose: Educó a sus hijos **para que** fueran independientes. B2|conj|Cuando, en cuanto, hasta que: indicative or subjunctive|294,4102,4236,4350,1375,1444,5889,6252,2274,689|Use the subjunctive when the time clause refers to the future; use the indicative for habits and facts.|After conjunctions of time (**cuando, en cuanto, hasta que, antes de que, tan pronto como, después de que**), the mood depends on whether the action is real or still to happen.¶T:Meaning¦Mood¦Example//habit or present fact¦indicative¦Solo llama **cuando necesita** algo. B2|conj|Siempre que: whenever or provided that|1497,4796,4821,6117|Siempre que + indicative means whenever; siempre que + subjunctive means provided that.|**Siempre que** has two meanings and the verb mood shows which one.¶T:Meaning¦Mood¦Example//whenever, every time that¦indicative (habit)¦Voy en bici **siempre que puedo**. B2|conj|Contrast: sin embargo, no obstante, en cambio, pese a|6061,6123,6124,6126,6127,6393,6121,6046|Use sin embargo, no obstante and en cambio to contrast, and pese a or a pesar de + noun to concede.|To contrast ideas in a more formal text use these connectors.¶T:Connector¦Meaning¦Example//**sin embargo**, **no obstante**¦however, nevertheless¦**Sin embargo**, hay que matizar que existen excepciones. B2|neg|Tag questions: ¿verdad?, ¿no?, ¿eh?|116,148,202,277|Add ¿verdad? or ¿no? to a statement to ask for confirmation; use ¿verdad? after a negative sentence.|Spanish has no change of verb for tags; just add a short word after a comma.¶• **¿no?** after an affirmative statement: Entonces eso significa que no vienes, **¿no?** (So that means you are not coming, right?) B2|mood|Subjunctive after feelings: me alegro de que|3681,3697,3813,3696,3814,3891|Verbs and expressions of feeling or judgement + que take the subjunctive when the subject changes.|After expressions of emotion, opinion or evaluation, the verb after **que** is in the **present subjunctive**.¶• Feelings: **Me alegro de que** estés aquí. (It is a shame you are not coming.) **Me parece bien que** seas sincero. (I think it is good that you are honest.) **Me parece genial que** me ayudes. (I think it is great that you are helping me.)¶• Need: No **hace falta que** estemos de acuerdo. (We do not have to agree.)¶Other triggers: me encanta que, me da pena que, es increíble que, es importante que, tengo miedo de que.¶Rules:¶• The subjunctive is used when the subject changes. If the subject is the same, use an infinitive: Me alegro de **estar** aquí (not me alegro de que estoy).¶• Some verbs add **de**: alegrarse **de que**, tener miedo **de que**. Never drop it before que with these verbs.¶• Compare with an opinion about facts: Creo que tienes razón (indicative).¶Tip: English speakers say I am glad you are here with an indicative; Spanish needs the subjunctive.
B2|mood|Subjunctive after wishes, requests and demands|3047,3036,1846,6326,6328,4582,6058,1442,6255,376|Verbs of wanting, asking, advising or allowing + que + different subject take the subjunctive.|When you want somebody else to do something, use **que + present subjunctive**.¶• Want: Solo **quiero que me asesoren**. (I just want them to advise me.) Los jóvenes **quieren que** se les **tome** en serio. (Young people want to be taken seriously.)¶• Ask, demand: **Exijo que me devuelvan** el dinero. (I demand a refund.) **Le ruego que me responda** antes del lunes. (Please reply before Monday.)¶• Suggest: Por eso **propongo que esperemos**. (That is why I suggest we wait.)¶• Allow: **Deja que** la salsa se **reduzca**. (Let the sauce reduce.) Ya no **dejo que** se **aprovechen** de mí. (I no longer let them take advantage of me.)¶• Wish someone well: **Le deseo que pase** una buena noche. (I wish you a pleasant evening.)¶T:Same subject¦Different subject//Quiero **salir**.¦Quiero que **salgas**.//Prefiero **esperar**.¦Prefiero que **esperes**.¶Verbs that work this way: querer, preferir, pedir, exigir, rogar, proponer, sugerir, recomendar, permitir, dejar, prohibir, aconsejar.¶Common mistake: with decir the mood depends on the meaning. Dice que viene (a statement, indicative) vs. Dice que vengas (an order, subjunctive).
B2|mood|Belief and doubt: creo que vs. dudo que|203,323,3671,3817,6044,3877,3714,3873,6131|Creo que and estoy seguro de que take the indicative; dudo que and puede que take the subjunctive.|The mood shows how sure the speaker is.¶T:Certainty¦Doubt//**creo que** + indicative¦**no creo que** + subjunctive//**estoy seguro de que** + indicative¦**dudo que** + subjunctive//**es verdad que** + indicative¦**puede que** / **es posible que** + subjunctive¶• Certainty: **Creo que** tienes razón. (I think you are right.) **Estoy seguro de que** saldrá bien. (I am sure it will go well.)¶• Doubt: **Dudo que** eso **funcione**. (I doubt that will work.) **Dudo mucho que** funcione. (I very much doubt it will work.)¶• Possibility: **Puede que** convenza a primera vista. (It may seem convincing at first sight.)¶Negating a verb of belief changes the mood: Creo que **te equivocas** vs. **No creo** que **te equivoques**. (I do not think you are wrong.)¶• In questions the choice follows the speaker: ¿Crees que **vendrá**? (neutral) vs. ¿Crees que **venga**? (less common).¶• Quizás and tal vez take the subjunctive for real doubt but the indicative when the speaker feels more certain.¶Tip: dudar que takes the subjunctive, but no dudo que is followed by the indicative (certainty): No dudo que **es** verdad.
B2|mood|Pretérito perfecto de subjuntivo: haya + participle|287,3700,3808,3809|Use haya + participle for a completed action in the subjunctive: Me alegro de que haya terminado.|The **pretérito perfecto de subjuntivo** is formed with the present subjunctive of haber (**haya, hayas, haya, hayamos, hayáis, hayan**) + participle. (I am glad everything went well.)¶• Me alegro de que **haya terminado**. (I am glad it is over.)¶• Me quedo tranquilo de que todo **haya salido** bien. (I am relieved that everything went well.)¶T:Not finished¦Finished//Me alegro de que **estés** aquí.¦Me alegro de que **hayas venido**.//Espero que **llegue**.¦Espero que **haya llegado**.¶• It also appears after doubts: Dudo que **haya llegado** a tiempo. (I doubt he arrived on time.)¶• And in future time clauses where the action will be complete first: Cuando **hayas terminado**, avísame. (When you have finished, tell me.)¶Tip: the participle never changes, and the pronoun goes before haya: Espero que se lo **hayas dicho**.
B2|mood|Imperfect subjunctive: ojalá, como si, quisiera|3664,4325,4326,3570,685,4319,308,317,6177,3008,794,5889|Use the imperfect subjunctive (-ra) for unreal wishes, como si, polite quisiera and after a past main verb.|The **imperfecto de subjuntivo** is built from the 3rd person plural preterite: hablaron to **hablara**, tuvieron to **tuviera**, pudieron to **pudiera**, fueron to **fuera**. (I wish I had more time.) ¡Si lo **hubiera sabido** antes! (If only I had known sooner!) Si **pudiera** volver atrás en el tiempo... (If I could turn back time ...)¶• After **como si**: Me siento **como si** me **hubiera pasado** un camión por encima. (I feel as if a truck had run me over.) Nos conocemos **como si** nos **hubiéramos parido**. (We know each other inside out.) Hay que vivir cada día **como si fuera** el último. (Live every day as if it were your last.)¶• Polite wish: **Quisiera** subrayar que esto es importante. (I would like to stress ...) No **quisiera** ser indiscreto. (I would not like to be indiscreet.)¶• After a past main verb (sequence of tenses): Educó a sus hijos **para que fueran** independientes. (She raised her children to be independent.) Eso fue **antes de que naciera** yo. (That was before I was born.) Quería que me **devolvieran** el dinero.¶Tip: the trigger is in the past or the conditional, so the subjunctive moves back to the imperfect.
B2|mood|Subjunctive in relative clauses: busco a alguien que|955,3147,3581,4597,5007,6020,708,4329|Use the subjunctive after que when the person or thing described is unknown, wished for or hypothetical.|In a relative clause the mood depends on whether the described person or thing is **known and real** (indicative) or **unknown, not yet existing or open** (subjunctive).¶T:Known (indicative)¦Unknown (subjunctive)//Tengo un piso que **tiene** balcón.¦Busco un piso que **tenga** balcón.//Conozco a alguien que **sabe** ruso.¦¿Conoces a alguien que **sepa** ruso?¶• Searching for something that may not exist: **Busco a alguien que se quede** con mi piso. (I am looking for someone to take over my flat.)¶• Negative or empty antecedent: Ya no compro nada que **pueda** pedir prestado. (I no longer buy anything I can borrow.)¶• Generalising statements: Eso no es algo que se **deba** dejar pasar. (That is nothing you should let slide.) La libertad no es algo que se **pueda** dar por sentado. (Freedom is not something that can be taken for granted.) La paz no es algo que se **pueda** dar por hecho.¶• Any time you like: Puedes acudir a mí **cuando quieras**. (You can come to me whenever you want.)¶• Fixed phrases: **lo que tenga que ser**, **sea lo que sea**, **cueste lo que cueste**. Lo que **tenga** que ser, será. (What will be will be.)¶Common mistake: use the indicative if the person exists: Busco a Ana, que **vive** aquí.
B2|mood|Passive with ser + participle|2607,5054,5285,5818,5945,6335,5788|Ser + participle (agreeing with the subject) makes a passive; the agent appears with por.|The **pasiva con ser** is formed with **ser** (in any tense) + **past participle**, which agrees in gender and number with the subject. (The film was awarded the Golden Bear.)¶• Lamentamos comunicarle que el puesto ya **ha sido cubierto**. (We regret to inform you that the post has been filled.)¶• With a modal: El arte expoliado debe **ser devuelto**. (Looted art must be returned.)¶Agent: La obra **fue escrita por** Lorca. (The play was written by Lorca.)¶Style: this passive is typical of news, official texts and formal writing. In speech Spanish prefers the active voice, the se passive (Se aprobó la ley) or an impersonal 3rd person (Han cancelado el vuelo).¶Do not confuse it with estar + participle, which describes a result: La tienda **está cerrada**. (The shop is closed.)
B2|mood|Pasiva refleja: se vende, se celebra|2132,4151,4400,1090,4575,4715,1556,3097,4549|Se + 3rd person verb agreeing with the thing is the usual passive in everyday Spanish.|The **pasiva refleja** has the form **se + verb in the 3rd person**, and the verb agrees with the grammatical subject (the thing).¶T:Singular¦Plural//**Se** celebra el torneo.¦**Se** celebran los torneos.//**Se** vende piso.¦**Se** venden pisos.¶• El torneo **se celebra** en verano. B2|numbers|Percentages, multiples and fractions: por ciento, el doble|2868,3188,3506,4974,5276,1101,5369,4339|Percent = X por ciento; el doble / el triple = twice / three times; un cuarto de hora = quarter of an hour.|• **Percentages**: un 20 **por ciento** (20 %), el diez **por ciento** más rico, **cien por cien** (100 %). B2|particles|Vale, claro, bueno: agreeing and reacting|29,32,103,265,266,3103,135,264|Short words like vale, claro and bueno signal agreement, understanding or a mild reaction.|These small words are heard in nearly every conversation in Spain.¶• **Vale** = okay. B2|particles|Por cierto, oye, en realidad, o sea: steering the talk|120,204,128,143,219,326,2354,400|Use these markers to change topic, correct, add a comment or restate what you mean.|Discourse markers guide the listener through a conversation.¶• **por cierto** = by the way, to add a side topic: **Por cierto**, tengo novedades. B2|punct|Inverted marks and question tags: ¿no?, ¿verdad?|116,148,202,277,1362,317,121,64,216,219|Open with ¿ or ¡ where the question or exclamation really begins; ¿no? and ¿verdad? close a statement.|Spanish always writes both marks: **¿** opens the question and **?** closes it; the same for **¡ !**¶• The opening mark goes where the question starts, not necessarily at the start of the sentence: Hablando de vacaciones, **¿adónde vas?** (Speaking of vacation, where are you going?) No quisiera ser indiscreto, pero **¿cuántos años tiene?**¶• Tag questions end a statement: Estás de broma, **¿no?** (You're joking, right?) Todavía no nos conocemos, **¿verdad?** (We haven't met yet, have we?)¶• Use a comma before the tag and the tag has its own ¿ ?: ¿Entonces no vienes, **¿no?**¶• Exclamations work the same way: Hemos tardado una eternidad, **¡qué lentos!**¶• After the closing mark you can continue without capital if the sentence goes on: ¿Cómo estás?, me preguntó.¶• Question words always carry an accent when they ask: ¿**Cuándo**? ¿**Qué**? See the next rule.¶• Do not put a full stop after ? or !¶Tip: English speakers often forget the opening mark; texting often drops it, but in formal writing it is mandatory.

B2|style|Reporting what others say: dice que, según|3270,335,2367,5269,3563,5485,6339,1585|Report speech with que + clause after decir, comentar or opinar, or use según + person.|To report information, use a reporting verb + **que** (no comma, no inverted commas).¶• Present reporting verb: the tense of the reported clause does not change: El médico **dice que** tengo que descansar. (The doctor says I have to rest.) Algunos **opinan que** el Estado no debería meterse en la economía. (Some say the state should stay out of the economy.)¶• Past reporting verb: the tense usually shifts back: **Comentó de pasada que** se muda. (He mentioned in passing that he is moving.) Dijo que **se mudaba** (he said he was moving); Dijo que **había llegado** (he said he had arrived).¶• Hearsay: El deporte es un asesinato, **dicen que dijo** Churchill. (Sport is murder, Churchill supposedly said.)¶• **Según + person/source** = according to: El resfriado masculino es un asunto muy serio, **según** los hombres. (Man flu is serious business, according to men.) **Según** los conocimientos actuales, no supone ningún riesgo. (According to current knowledge it poses no risk.) Según lo acordado, haremos la entrega antes del viernes. (As agreed, we will deliver before Friday.)¶Direct speech uses a dash or inverted commas: Invita la casa, dijo el camarero. (It is on the house, said the waiter.)¶Tip: after según do not add que unless it means as: según dice el director.
B2|style|Structuring an argument: en primer lugar, por último, en resumen|6046,6051,6052,6054,6055,6110,6135,6147,6211|Order your points with fixed connectors: en primer lugar, además, por último, en resumen.|In essays, talks and formal emails use connectors to show the structure of your argument.¶T:Step¦Connector¦Example//start¦**en primer lugar**¦**En primer lugar**, quisiera subrayar que esto es importante. (First, I would like to stress ...)//add¦**además**, **por otro lado**¦**Además**, hay que tener en cuenta que lleva su tiempo. (Moreover, ...)//contrast¦**por un lado ... por otro**¦**Por un lado** es caro, pero **por otro** se ahorra tiempo. (On the one hand ... on the other ...)//last point¦**por último**¦**Por último**, pero no menos importante, se trata de justicia. (Last but not least ...)//conclusion¦**en resumen**, **en definitiva**¦**En resumen**, se puede decir que merece la pena. (In summary, ...)//reason¦**al fin y al cabo**¦**Al fin y al cabo**, es una cuestión de prioridades. (Ultimately, ...)¶• Each of these connectors starts the sentence and is followed by a comma.¶• Further options: **por lo tanto** (therefore), **así que** (so), **por eso** (that is why), **para terminar** (to conclude): **Para terminar**, quisiera destacar lo importante que es esto.¶Tip: do not use all the connectors at once. Pick one for each step of your argument. Use además plus a new idea, never to repeat the same one.
C1|tenses|Future for predictions and verdicts on history|4578,4856,4881,4948,6029,6031,4330,4172,4135|Use the simple future for confident predictions and judgements about what time or history will show.|At C1 the future is not only "what I will do". Writers and speakers use it to make a confident forecast or to say how later generations will judge something.¶• **Predictions:** Regiones enteras se volverán inhabitables. (Entire regions will become uninhabitable.)¶• **Verdicts of history:** Algún día se recordará esta época. (People will look back on this time one day.)¶• **Evaluation:** Renunciar a cosas no será suficiente. (Doing without alone won't be enough.)¶• **Set phrases:** El tiempo lo dirá. (Time will tell.) Mañana será otro día. (Tomorrow is another day.)¶The future also expresses probability about the present: **Serán las diez** (It must be about ten), **Estará en casa** (He is probably at home). Context decides whether it is a forecast or a guess.¶Tip for English speakers: Spanish keeps the future for firm statements about the world, while plans among people are often expressed with ir a + infinitive or the present (Mañana voy a verlo).¶Do not use the future after si (if) in conditions: Si hace buen tiempo, saldremos, not si hará.
C1|tenses|Ya + future: postponing, reassuring, conceding|164,3348,4197,4272,6364,6380,6391,6403|Ya + future promises or concedes something without committing: Ya veremos, Ya te diré algo.|In everyday Spain Spanish, ya combined with the future is not about time at all. (I'll get back to you on that.)¶• **Reassuring:** Ya verás como todo sale bien. (You'll see, everything will turn out fine.) Ya se pasará. (It will pass.)¶• **Promising vaguely:** Ya sacaré tiempo para eso. (I'll find the time for that, somehow.)¶• **Open outcome:** Eso ya se verá. (That remains to be seen.) Ya nos veremos. (See you around.)¶The speaker often means "not now, and I make no promise about when". Depending on intonation, Ya veremos can also be a polite refusal, much like English "we'll see".¶Do not confuse it with ya meaning already (Ya he comido). With the future, ya is a pragmatic marker and is hard to translate word for word.
C1|tenses|Conditional for hypotheses, wishes and exaggeration|1530,3847,3944,3391,3480,5872,6156,6157,711,4323|The conditional states what would be: imagined situations, vivid wishes and exaggerations, cautious judgements.|Beyond politeness (Me gustaría...), the conditional builds imagined scenes and softens judgements.¶• **Vivid exaggeration:** Me comería un caballo. (Without music, life would be a mistake.)¶• **Cautious evaluation:** Sería fatal ignorarlo. (It would be fatal to ignore that.) Sería un error concluir de ello que todo va bien. (It would be wrong to conclude that everything is fine.)¶• **Proverbs:** Una manzana al día, del médico te libraría. (An apple a day keeps the doctor away.)¶• **Looking back:** Echando la vista atrás, haría muchas cosas de otra manera. (Looking back, I would do a lot differently.)¶The condition is often only implied (if I could, if it were allowed). Written Spanish also uses the conditional to report an unconfirmed fact: El presidente habría dicho... (The president reportedly said...), typical of press style.¶Remember that the conditional is never used after si in the if-clause: that slot takes the imperfect subjunctive.
C1|tenses|Imperfect of politeness and softened statements|150,234,252,548,3032,171,253,3961|The imperfect (quería, pensaba) distances a wish or opinion from the present and sounds more polite or tentative.|Spanish often uses the imperfect where English uses "I was wondering" or "I'd like". (I'd like to file a complaint.)¶• **Softened intention:** Otra cosa que quería decirte: gracias por lo de ayer. (Another thing I wanted to say: thanks for yesterday.)¶• **Excusing yourself:** No quería interrumpirte. (I didn't mean to interrupt you.) No quería ser maleducado. (I didn't mean to be rude.)¶• **Recalling what was meant:** A eso me refería. (That's what I was getting at.) ¿Cómo te lo diría? (How should I put it?)¶• **Disappointed expectations:** Me esperaba más. (I expected more from it.)¶The action is not really in the past: Quería pedirle un favor means "I want to ask you a favour now". Compare the blunter Quiero pedirle un favor. C1|order|Left dislocation: La confianza hay que ganársela|785,3587,4302,4556,6034,1172,599,637,1084,1490,1150,4581|Put the object first as topic and repeat it with lo/la/los/las: La receta hay que usarla.|Spanish loves to start with what you are talking about (the topic) and then comment on it. When a direct or indirect object is moved to the front, a pronoun repeats it in the verb phrase.¶• La confianza hay que ganársela. (Trust has to be earned.)¶• La receta hay que usarla en un plazo de 28 días. (The prescription must be filled within 28 days.)¶• Esas imágenes no las olvidaré nunca. (I will never forget these pictures.)¶• Las sobras las congelo. (I freeze the leftovers.)¶• Esta te la debo. (I owe you this one.)¶• Eso no lo pienso consentir. (I won't put up with that.)¶Indirect objects behave the same: A los vecinos de toda la vida los están echando. (They are driving out long-standing neighbours.) A los jóvenes se les suele subestimar.¶The pronoun is compulsory when the object is known and comes first; without it the sentence sounds wrong (not La receta hay que usar). Compare the neutral order: Hay que usar la receta en 28 días.¶Use it to contrast topics, to sound natural in speech, and to link to what was just said.¶In English the same effect needs passive or stress: "Trust, you have to earn."
C1|order|Verb before subject: Se me ha despertado el gusanillo|5083,2355,2325,2364,2374,2329,4436,1533,1465|With feelings, reactions and new information the subject often comes after the verb.|Spanish word order is flexible: the subject can follow the verb, especially when it is new information or the verb expresses an impression, a feeling or an event.¶• A las palabras tienen que seguir los hechos. (Words must be followed by deeds.)¶• Me duelen músculos que ni sabía que tenía. (I have aches in muscles I didn't know I had.)¶• Le falló la cabeza en el momento decisivo. (His head failed him at the critical moment.)¶• Se les notaba la decepción en la cara. (The disappointment showed on their faces.)¶• Se me ha despertado el gusanillo de la competición. (The competitive bug has bitten me.)¶• A los jóvenes les importa conciliar trabajo y vida personal. (Work-life balance matters to young people.)¶Rule of thumb: the longer or more important part comes last (end focus). Gustar-type verbs, verbs of appearance (surgir, ocurrir, faltar) and structures with se follow this pattern.¶Placing the subject first is not wrong but it changes the emphasis: La victoria se le ha subido a la cabeza (the topic is the win).¶English speakers tend to put the subject first every time. C1|order|Focus with lo que, quien and donde clauses|4907,6096,4360,5306,4963,5163,6015,6267,6010,4527|Start with Quien... / Lo que... / Donde... to stress an idea or state a general truth.|Relative clauses that act as the subject of the sentence give statements weight, rhythm and proverb-like emphasis.¶• **Quien + verb (any person who):** Quien no innova se queda atrás. (What it is really about is funding.)¶• **Donde:** Donde antes estaba la franja de la muerte, hoy hay un parque. (Where the death strip used to be, there is now a park.)¶• **Ser + clause (focus):** Bajo presión es cuando mejor trabajo. (I work best under pressure.) La esperanza es lo último que se pierde. (Hope dies last.)¶Quien takes a singular verb even when it means "people who" (Quien no vota deja que otros decidan). Use el que/la que/los que when you need gender and number.¶Tip: where English says "It is X that...", Spanish often uses ser + relative with the same word: Es aquí donde, Es entonces cuando.¶After the verb ser the focused element comes second: this reverses normal order and highlights it.

C1|modal|Hay que, hace falta, habría que: impersonal necessity|785,1505,2717,3389,4467,4472,4525,4601,4677,4689|Hay que + infinitive and hace falta + noun state general necessity without naming who must act.|When the duty belongs to everybody or nobody in particular, Spanish avoids a subject.¶• **Hay que + infinitive:** Hay que reservar con semanas de antelación. C1|modal|Debería and podría: ideals, opinions and possibility|4367,4514,5269,5584,6103,6244,5234,5404,5413,6084|Debería states what ought to be; podría states what could be true or happen.|In debates and essays the conditionals of deber and poder do most of the modal work.¶**Debería + infinitive** = ought to, an ideal or a criticism of how things are:¶• El bien común debería ser lo primero. C1|articles|Neuter lo: lo + adjective, lo que, lo de|189,357,369,673,737,788,793,999,252,6096|Lo makes abstract nouns: lo importante, lo que digo, lo de ayer, lo más + adjective.|The neuter article **lo** never goes before a noun. C1|articles|Todo un / toda una + noun (emphatic)|228,1538,1775,2538,3041,4429,5628,6035,1132|Todo un + noun means 'a real, a true': todo un éxito, todo un reto.|Before a singular noun, **todo un / toda una** does not mean 'all of a'. C1|articles|Generic nouns: article or no article?|135,397,1174,1597,1727,3815,6067,694,3098,5157|Use the article for generic ideas as subject (la vida); drop it after tener, con, sin and in set phrases.|Spanish uses the definite article for general or abstract nouns as subject, where English uses none.¶• **La** vida es bella. (People don't try what they don't know.)¶The article is dropped in these cases:¶• after **tener** with an abstract noun and no adjective: tienes **razón**, tengo **ganas**, tener **hambre**;¶• after **sin** and often **con**: **sin** dinero, **con** paciencia;¶• in many fixed expressions: **por** casualidad, **en** opinión de, **a** mano;¶• with professions and roles after ser, hacerse, como: va a ser **padre**; trabaja **como** profesora.¶If you add an adjective or a modifier, the article returns: tengo **un** hambre de lobo (I'm ravenous). Common mistake: dropping the article in subjects (say La paciencia es importante, not Paciencia es importante).
C1|nouns|Nouns that change meaning with gender|1086,1851,4469,4768,5002,5088,5101,5919,5999,4744|El orden / la orden, el editorial / la editorial: the article decides the meaning.|A group of nouns has the same form but two genders, and each gender has a different meaning. The article is the key.¶T:Masculine¦Feminine//el orden (order, tidiness)¦la orden (command, order)//el editorial (editorial article)¦la editorial (publishing house)//el capital (money)¦la capital (capital city)//el cura (priest)¦la cura (cure)//el frente (front)¦la frente (forehead)//el policía (police officer)¦la policía (the police force)//el radio (radius)¦la radio (radio)//el margen (margin, space)¦la margen (river bank)¶• **El orden** mundial está cambiando. (The world order is changing.)¶• Está **a la orden** del día. (It is on the agenda / an everyday reality.)¶• **La policía** está investigando. (The police are investigating.)¶Note: for a police officer, el/la policía both exist (el policía = male, la policía = female officer or the force). Learn each pair with its article.
C1|nouns|Diminutives and augmentatives (-ito, -illo, -ón, -azo)|1072,1182,1440,1531,1584,2309,1693,909|Suffixes add size or feeling: casita (little, cosy), golazo (great goal), pajarito.|Spanish adds suffixes to nouns for size, affection, irony or praise. At C1 you should read the nuance.¶• **-ito / -ita** (-cito, -ecito after n, r, e): **jardincito**, **casita**, **pajarito**, **chorrito**. Affection or small size: Él come como un **pajarito**. (He eats like a bird.) In Spain -ito is the standard; -illo/-illa is also common (**chupito**, a shot).¶• **-ón / -ona**: bigger or more intense, often with a gender change: **cucharón** (ladle).¶• **-azo / -aza**: a blow or an impressive example: **golazo** (a great goal), **cochazo** (a fantastic car), **codazo** (an elbow jab).¶• **-ucho / -ote / -aco**: pejorative: **casucha** (a hovel), **animalucho**.¶Spelling changes: poco → **poquito**, café → **cafecito**, Pablo → **Pablito**. Diminutives also soften requests and orders: Espera un **momentito**. Do not create them for every noun; learners overuse them. Adjectives and adverbs take them too: **cerquita** (very near).
C1|nouns|Collective nouns and verb agreement|5086,5783,5821,2533,2670,4424,6035,3125|La mayoría de, un montón de, la gente: singular noun, but the verb may agree with the meaning.|Collective nouns name a group in the singular (**la gente**, **el grupo**, **la mayoría**). The grammar is singular, but Spanish allows agreement by meaning in some cases.¶• **La gente** es amable. (People are friendly.) **La gente** is always singular: la gente de aquí **es** muy amable. Never say las gentes for people in general.¶• **La mayoría de** + plural noun: the verb can be singular or plural, and the plural is common when the noun is close: La mayoría de los objetivos **no se han cumplido**. (Most goals were not met.) The singular is also correct.¶• **Un montón de, una serie de, un grupo de, la mitad de**: Un montón de público **atrae**/**atraen**. Strict style prefers the verb with the first noun; both are accepted.¶• **Millones de personas** takes a plural verb: Millones de personas **han huido**.¶• Adjectives follow the collective noun's gender: la gente **cansada**.¶Tip: in writing, keep the verb in the singular after a collective noun when the idea is one block, and in the plural when you picture the individuals.
C1|pronouns|Double clitics: se lo, me lo, order of pronouns|534,1841,2910,310,755,1579,1172,5212|Indirect before direct (me lo, te la); le/les + lo/la/los/las becomes se lo, se la.|When two object pronouns appear together, the order is fixed: **reflexive/se, then indirect, then direct**. Mnemonic: RID.¶• Indirect before direct: **me lo** dio, **te la** mando, **nos los** trajo. (He gave it to me; I'll send it to you; he brought them to us.)¶• **le / les + lo, la, los, las → se lo, se la...** (two l-words never stand together): Ya **se lo** he dicho. (I've already told him/her/them.) Se lo agradezco mucho. (I'm very grateful for that.)¶• The pronoun **se** here has nothing to do with the reflexive se. To clarify who: **Se lo** dije **a ella**.¶• Position: before a conjugated verb, but attached to infinitive, gerund and positive imperative: Quiero decír**selo**. / **Se lo** quiero decir. Dámelo. (Give it to me.) Add a written accent to keep the stress: dándo**selo**, díse**lo**.¶• Never put a pronoun between two verbs of a compound: **Se lo** he dicho, not He se lo dicho.¶Common mistake: pluralising se when the recipient is plural (say Se lo di a ellos, not Se los di a ellos). Only the object pronoun agrees with the thing given: Se **las** di (the things, feminine plural).
C1|pronouns|Idioms with se + lo/la: tomárselo, pensárselo|1940,5212,1172,755,1579,1571,310|Fixed verb + se lo/la expressions where lo/la has no clear noun: tomárselo con calma.|Many idioms contain a pronoun that stands for no specific thing. They are learned as blocks.¶• **tomárselo con calma** (take it easy): Se **lo** toma con mucha calma.¶• **pensárselo dos veces** (think twice): Las empresas se **lo** piensan dos veces.¶• **echárselo en cara** (throw it in someone's face): Todavía se **lo** echa en cara.¶• **llevárselo todo / pasárselo bien** (have a good time): Nos **lo** pasamos genial.¶• **Cargárselo, montárselo, currárselo, ganárselo**: Se **lo** ha currado mucho. (He has worked hard for it.)¶A related pattern is the dative of involuntary action or interest: **Se le** ha ido la mano (He overdid it); **Se me** ha caído el vaso (The glass slipped out of my hands). The speaker presents the action as unintentional and the owner as affected.¶Another pattern is passive-looking: La llave **se la** ha tragado la tierra. (The key has vanished off the face of the earth.)¶Tip: look up the whole phrase in a dictionary under the verb, because lo/la is part of the idiom. Without it the meaning changes: tomar con calma means almost the same, but sounds neutral and less colloquial.
C1|pronouns|Relative pronouns: quien, el que, el cual, cuyo|1785,2791,4191,4448,4962,5231,6020,704,4853,6389|After prepositions use el que/el cual/quien; quien alone means whoever, he who.|Beyond que, C1 requires the full set of relatives.¶• **quien / quienes** (people only; no gender): **Quien** viaja tiene mucho que contar. (Whoever travels has a lot to tell.) Proverbs use it: **A quien** madruga, Dios le ayuda.¶• **el que / la que / los que / las que**: after prepositions, or as 'the one who': La libertad **de la que** disfrutamos... (The freedom we enjoy...). Los países del Sur son **los que** más sufren. (the ones who)¶• **el cual / la cual / los cuales / las cuales** (formal, written): used after longer prepositions and in non-restrictive clauses: El proyecto, **el cual** fue aprobado, ... **Lo cual** refers to a whole idea.¶• **cuyo / cuya / cuyos / cuyas** (whose) agrees with the thing possessed, not the owner: la autora **cuyos** libros leo (the author whose books I read).¶• **lo que** (what) is the neuter form: no digas **lo que** piensas.¶Mistake: using que after a preposition for a person (La chica con que hablé). Say con **quien** or con **la que**. Commas before the clause mean it is non-restrictive: add information, not identify.
C1|pronouns|Impersonal uno: you, one|3982,4292,4951,5835,5988,6222,6232,281|Uno + 3rd person singular means you / one: Con el tiempo uno se acostumbra.|**Uno** (feminine **una** when a woman speaks about herself) is a general 'you' or 'one', often with a hint that the speaker includes himself/herself.¶• **Uno** no da crédito a lo que ve. (You can't believe your eyes.)¶• Con la edad **uno** se vuelve más tranquilo. (With age you become calmer.)¶• **Uno** crece con los retos. (You grow with challenges.)¶• Cuidar el medio ambiente empieza por **uno mismo**. (...starts with yourself.)¶How it differs from other impersonals:¶T:Form¦Nuance//**se** + verb¦neutral, no speaker: Se vive bien aquí.//**uno** + verb¦speaker included, personal: Uno vive bien aquí.//**tú** + verb¦colloquial, direct: Vives bien aquí.//**la gente**¦people in general, speaker excluded¶Use **uno** especially for feelings and personal experiences. Pronoun forms: **a uno** (me gusta que **te** respeten a **uno**), **de uno** (el sitio de uno), **uno mismo** for emphasis. In English, translate with 'you' or 'one' (more formal).
C1|pronouns|Strong reflexives: sí, consigo, sí mismo|2183,2349,4807,5248,5272,5459,4951|After prepositions, 3rd-person reflexive is sí/consigo: por sí solo, a sí mismo, hablar consigo.|After a preposition the reflexive for the third person (singular and plural) is **sí**, and with **con** it is **consigo**. For the first and second person nothing changes (**mí, ti**, conmigo, contigo).¶• Se ha superado **a sí mismo**. (He surpassed himself.) Me he superado **a mí mismo**.¶• Las cifras hablan **por sí solas**. (The figures speak for themselves.)¶• El crecimiento no es un fin **en sí mismo**. (...an end in itself.)¶• Reciclar no basta **por sí solo**. (Recycling alone isn't enough.)¶• Lleva el pasaporte **consigo**. (He carries his passport with him.)¶**mismo** and **solo** agree with the subject in gender and number: ella **por sí misma**, ellos **por sí solos**. The subject must be the same: Pedro habló de **sí** (of himself) vs. Pedro habló de **él** (of someone else).¶Do not confuse **sí** (pronoun, with accent) with **si** (if) and **sí** (yes). Tip for English speakers: English uses himself/themselves; Spanish needs the preposition + sí: 'by itself' = por sí solo.
C1|pronouns|Cualquier(a), quienquiera, cualquier + noun|337,2779,4194,4697,5137,6387,4884,3591|Cualquier before a noun, cualquiera alone or after the noun; whoever needs the subjunctive.|**Cualquier** means 'any (at all)'. It loses the final -a before a singular noun (masculine or feminine): **cualquier** caso, **cualquier** cosa. Plural **cualesquiera** is rare; use cualquier with a plural idea carefully.¶• **Cualquier** + noun: En **cualquier** caso, deberíamos empezar. (In any case, we should begin.) Puedo trabajar desde **cualquier** sitio.¶• **cualquiera** (pronoun, after the noun, or alone): un día como otro **cualquiera** (a day like any other); **Cualquiera** puede ser un medio de comunicación. (Anyone can be a broadcaster.)¶• **Cualquiera** can be a negative colloquial: ¡**Cualquiera** lo sabe! (Who could know?) or a person: no ser **cualquiera** (not an ordinary person).¶• **Quienquiera**, **dondequiera**, **cuandoquiera** + que + subjunctive: **Quienquiera que** lo haya hecho... In negative sentences use **ningún** instead: sin **ningún** problema.
C1|pronouns|Algún, ningún, nadie, cada uno, todo el mundo|219,1592,997,1000,1800,568,3999,4562,1151,1327,1534|Algún/ningún shorten before masculine nouns; nadie and ninguno need no before the verb.|Indefinites and quantifiers need agreement and correct negation.¶• **alguno → algún**, **ninguno → ningún** before a masculine singular noun: ¿Tienes **algún** plan? Before a feminine noun with stressed a- the full form is usual: ninguna alma (or ningún alma, accepted).¶• **Nadie** (nobody) and **ninguno** follow the double negation rule: **No** conozco a **nadie**. / **Nadie** me ha llamado. C1|adjectives|Adjective position changes meaning|1187,1097,2732,201,2255,681,780,789,2248,1569,2542,350|Before the noun: figurative or inherent sense; after: literal or distinguishing.|Many adjectives have two positions. C1|adjectives|Absolute superlatives: -ísimo and intensifiers|334,545,1033,1092,1345,1389,1419,2105,2692,3125,3788|-ísimo means extremely: buenísimo, carísimo; also muy, super-, re-, lo más.|The absolute superlative expresses a very high degree, without comparing.¶• **-ísimo/-ísima**: adjectives and some adverbs. Drop the final vowel: fácil → **facilísima**; caro → **carísimo**; bueno → **buenísima**. The adjective agrees: Los ingredientes son de **primerísima** calidad.¶• Spelling changes: rico → **riquísimo**, largo → **larguísimo**, feliz → **felicísimo**, joven → **jovencísimo**. Irregular and Latin forms: amable → **amabilísimo**, antiguo → **antiquísimo**, fiel → **fidelísimo**.¶• Quantifiers: **muchísimo** (very much), **muchísima** luz, **tardísimo**, **cerquísima**.¶• Alternatives: **muy** + adjective; prefixes **super-**, **re-**, **requete-**, **archi-**, **ultra-**; **de lo más** + adjective; adverbs like **sumamente**; repetition (grande, grande).¶• Estoy **cabreadísimo**. (I'm furious.) Está **carísimo** para lo que es. (It's far too expensive.)¶Do not use **muy** + -ísimo (muy buenísimo). Words that already mean the maximum (enorme, fantástico) rarely take it.
C1|adjectives|Comparisons: más de lo que, cuanto más, tanto como|4270,4779,5503,5515,6114,6115,5990,6111,3380,6296|Más/menos de lo que + clause; cuanto más..., más...; tanto...como; ni la sombra de lo que.|Beyond más que, C1 needs comparisons with clauses and proportional ones.¶• **más/menos + de lo que** (compared with a whole clause): Nos creemos más racionales **de lo que** somos. (...than we are.) Escribimos más **de lo que** llamamos.¶• **de lo que / del que / de la que / de los que** depend on the thing compared: Tiene más dinero **del que** necesita. (He has more money than he needs.) Compare: Tiene más dinero que su hermano (a noun).¶• **Cuanto más / menos..., más / menos...** (the more..., the more...): **Cuanto más** lo piensas, **más** complicado se vuelve. With adjectives: Cuanto mayor es el riesgo, menor es la ganancia. Add **mientras / a medida que** as alternatives: Mientras más grande, mejor (Latin America).¶• **tanto...como** = both...and: Me siento extranjero **tanto** aquí **como** allí. **tan...como** is for adjectives and adverbs.¶• Expression of degrees: **ni la sombra de lo que era** (not a shadow of what he was).¶Tip: In English 'than' links both; Spanish uses **de lo que** with a verb. Remember the double comparative with **más...más** only with cuanto.
C1|preps|Prepositional phrases for formal writing|2646,3896,4744,5012,6105,6106,6107,6393,4600,3874,4269|En cuanto a, respecto a, de cara a, a raíz de, debido a: formal ways to link topics and causes.|Formal Spanish uses fixed phrases ending in a preposition. Learn the whole block.¶• **En cuanto a / con respecto a / respecto a / por lo que respecta a** = regarding: **En cuanto a** la financiación, aún quedan cosas por aclarar. **Respecto a** su pregunta, puedo decirle lo siguiente.¶• **De cara a** = with a view to, facing: **De cara al** futuro, tenemos que cambiar. (Note a + el = al.)¶• **Debido a / a causa de / a raíz de / gracias a / por culpa de** = cause: **Debido a** una avería... **Gracias a** los pódcasts... (positive cause). **Por culpa de** is negative.¶• **A través de / mediante / por medio de** = through, by means of: Me informo **a través de** distintas fuentes.¶• **A pesar de / pese a / aun así** = despite: **A pesar de** todo, la vida es bella.¶• **Con vistas a / en torno a / a lo largo de / en función de**: El precio cambia **en función de** la demanda.¶Grammar: these phrases take a noun or an infinitive. For a clause use a conjunction: **a pesar de que**, **debido a que**. Do not say debido que or a pesar que (an error from Latin American Spanish is common but avoid it).
C1|preps|Verbs with fixed prepositions (régimen preposicional)|492,4418,4728,4881,4925,4927,5226,6390,5620,4555|Learn verb + preposition pairs: depender de, contar con, renunciar a, confiar en, tratarse de.|Many verbs require a specific preposition that English does not predict. Learn them together.¶T:Preposition¦Verbs and examples//**de**¦depender de (**Depender de** las importaciones es un error.), carecer de, fiarse de, darse cuenta de, tratarse de, acordarse de//**con**¦contar con (Siempre puedo **contar con** ella.), soñar con, acabar con, enfrentarse con, conformarse con//**a**¦renunciar a (Renunciar **a** cosas no basta.), aspirar a, dedicarse a, enfrentarse a, negarse a//**en**¦confiar en (He aprendido a **confiar en** la vida.), insistir en, consistir en, basarse en, pensar en//**por**¦optar por, preocuparse por, interesarse por¶The preposition stays with the verb in clauses: Depende **de que** vengas (not Depende que). **Dequeísmo** (adding de when it is wrong: Pienso de que) and **queísmo** (dropping it: Me alegro que) are common errors. Test: change the clause to 'eso': Me alegro **de eso** → me alegro **de que**. Pienso **eso** → pienso que.¶With some verbs both are possible with a change in meaning: pensar **en** (to think about someone) vs. pensar **de** (to have an opinion).
C1|preps|Personal a: advanced uses|955,1335,3567,3999,4562,5772,5991|Add a before a specific person or pet direct object, and before nadie, alguien, alguno.|The **personal a** marks a direct object that is a specific person (or personified being). It has no English equivalent.¶• **Always** before indefinite pronouns that refer to people: No quiero contagiar **a nadie**. Las generalizaciones no ayudan **a nadie**. Preguntar **a alguien**...¶• Before a specific person, a pet or something personified: Busco **a** mi hermano. La guerra mató **a** miles. Quiere mucho **a** su perro.¶• **Not used** with non-specific people: Busco un médico (any doctor) vs. Busco **a** un médico que me recomendaron (a particular one). Busco **a alguien** que se quede con mi piso (the subjunctive says the person is unidentified, but a stays with alguien).¶• **Not with tener**: Tengo dos hermanos. But Tengo **a** mi madre enferma (resultative).¶• Used with things to avoid ambiguity: El otoño sigue **al** verano. Vencer **al** miedo.¶• Avoid the sequence a + a: Vi a la gente (not twice).¶Common mistake: dropping a with nadie (No veo nadie is wrong). Another: adding a with indefinite things: Veo a un coche is wrong.
C1|conj|Concession: aunque, si bien, pese a, a pesar de|6121,6122,6123,6124,6393,2694,3565,4741|Concessive links (aunque, si bien, pese a) introduce what contrasts with the main idea but does not cancel it.|Concessive connectors admit a fact and then state the opposing one.¶• **Aunque + indicative** (the fact is real): Aunque las cifras pintan bien, sigo siendo prudente. (Although the figures look good, I remain cautious.)¶• **Si bien + indicative** (formal): Si bien el objetivo es correcto, el camino es equivocado. (While the goal is right, the path is wrong.)¶• **Pese a / a pesar de + noun or infinitive:** Pese a las críticas, el Gobierno mantiene el plan. (Despite the criticism, the government is sticking to the plan.) La vida es bella, a pesar de todo. (Life is beautiful, despite everything.)¶• **Aun así** (even so) starts a new sentence: Aun así, voy a trabajar arrastrándome. (Even so, I'll drag myself to work.)¶• **Y eso que + indicative** (even though; colloquial): Ya tengo ganas de volver a viajar, y eso que acabo de llegar.¶Use **aunque + subjunctive** when the fact is hypothetical or the speaker does not care: Aunque llueva, saldremos. (Even if it rains, we'll go out.)¶Pese a que and a pesar de que take a clause: Pese a que lo intentó, no lo logró.¶Never combine aunque with pero in the same clause chain: write Aunque es caro, lo compro, not ...pero lo compro.
C1|conj|Conditions: a no ser que, siempre que, con la condición de que|178,6116,6117,6118,6120,6331,5146,4796|These links set a condition; most require the subjunctive (a no ser que, siempre que, con la condición de que).|Beyond si, formal Spanish has several ways to impose conditions.¶• **A no ser que + subjunctive** (unless): A no ser que tengas una idea mejor. (Unless you have a better idea.) A no ser que encontremos una solución mejor.¶• **Siempre que + subjunctive** (provided that): Siempre que todos participen, puede salir bien. (Provided everyone takes part, it can work.)¶• **Con la condición de que + subjunctive:** Con la condición de que se cubran los costes, estoy de acuerdo. (On condition that the costs are covered, I agree.)¶• **En caso de + noun:** En caso de fracaso, la responsabilidad es nuestra. (In the event of failure, the responsibility is ours.) En caso de duda, a favor del acusado.¶• **De lo contrario** (otherwise): De lo contrario, me veré obligado a emprender acciones legales.¶Beware of siempre que with the indicative, which means "whenever": Voy en bici siempre que puedo. (I cycle whenever I can.)¶Similar links: con tal de que, siempre y cuando, salvo que, a menos que. All take the subjunctive.¶Do not put the future or conditional after these connectors. Use the present or imperfect subjunctive depending on the main verb.
C1|conj|Consequence: por consiguiente, por lo tanto, de ahí, así que|6139,6140,6141,6099,6385,1120,6142|Consequence connectors (por consiguiente, por lo tanto, así que, de ahí) draw a conclusion from what was said.|Several connectors express a result, ranging from formal to casual.¶• **Por consiguiente / por lo tanto / como consecuencia** (formal): Por consiguiente, tenemos que replantearnos las cosas. (Consequently, we have to rethink things.) Como consecuencia, subieron los precios. (As a result, prices went up.)¶• **Así que / de modo que** (neutral, spoken): Solo se vive una vez, ¡así que adelante! (You only live once, so go for it!)¶• **De ahí** (from there it follows): De ahí surge la pregunta de si es justo. (From this the question arises whether it is fair.) De ahí que + subjunctive is the standard formula: Hay poco tiempo; de ahí que debamos priorizar.¶• **Tan + adjective + que:** Las paredes son tan finas que se oye todo. (The walls are so thin that you can hear everything.)¶• **Así queda demostrado que:** Así queda demostrado que funciona. (This shows that it works.)¶Punctuation: put a comma after por consiguiente and por lo tanto when they open the sentence.¶Remember: por eso and por ello are used for reasons already given. De ahí que is reserved for conclusions and takes the subjunctive.
C1|conj|Reasons: dada la situación, debido a, gracias a|6103,6104,4744,2646,250,6146,2758|Formal reasons use dado/a, debido a, gracias a or a gerund; ya que gives a known reason.|Spanish distinguishes the nature of the reason by the connector.¶• **Dado/a + noun:** Dada la situación, deberíamos ser prudentes. (In view of the situation, we should be cautious.)¶• **Teniendo en cuenta + noun** (taking into account): Teniendo en cuenta los costes, eso es difícilmente justificable.¶• **Debido a + noun** (neutral/negative cause): Debido a una avería en la señalización, el tren sufrirá un retraso. (Due to a signal failure, the train will be delayed.)¶• **Gracias a + noun** (positive cause): La radio está viviendo un renacimiento gracias a los pódcasts. (Radio is having a renaissance thanks to podcasts.)¶• **Ya que** (since, a reason the listener knows): Ya que estamos: ¿tienes mi llave? (While we're at it: do you have my key?)¶• **Porque** (the straightforward reason): Metí la pata porque no conocía las costumbres.¶• **No en vano** (not without reason): No en vano el tema es tan delicado. (It is not for nothing that the subject is so delicate.)¶Debido a and gracias a are followed by nouns, not conjugated verbs; add que for a clause: debido a que, gracias a que. Puesto que and dado que are formal equivalents of ya que.
C1|conj|Pairs and parallels: cuanto más, no solo, tanto como|6110,6111,6112,6113,6114,6115|Correlative pairs link two parts: cuanto más..., más...; por un lado..., por otro...; tanto... como...|Correlatives structure an argument and balance two ideas.¶• **Cuanto más/menos..., más/menos...** (the more..., the more...): Cuanto más lo piensas, más complicado se vuelve. (The more you think, the more complicated it gets.) Cuanto más esperemos, más caro saldrá. (With a future meaning, the subjunctive appears.)¶• **Por un lado..., por otro...:** Por un lado se ahorra dinero y por otro se protege el medio ambiente. (On the one hand money is saved, on the other the environment is protected.)¶• **Tanto... como...:** Merece la pena tanto desde el punto de vista ecológico como desde el económico. (It is worthwhile both ecologically and economically.)¶• **No solo..., sino también...:** No solo los costes, sino también el esfuerzo es enorme. (Not only the costs but also the effort is enormous.)¶• **Ni... ni...:** Ni una ni otra solución es perfecta. (Neither solution is perfect.)¶Agreement: with tanto... como the verb is plural when both elements are subjects; with ni... ni the verb follows the second item or the plural.¶Keep parallel forms: if the first part has a noun phrase, so should the second.¶In the negative, ni... ni replaces o... o: No tengo ni tiempo ni dinero.
C1|neg|No es X, sino Y: correcting with sino and sino que|1185,5692,5796,5987,6024,6097,6113|After a negative, sino introduces the correct alternative; use sino que before a conjugated verb.|Sino (written as one word) corrects or replaces a negated element: "not this, but that".¶• No es la casa, sino la gente que vive en ella. (Home isn't a place but a feeling.)¶• La pregunta no es si, sino cómo. (The question isn't whether, but how.)¶• **No solo... sino también:** No solo los costes, sino también el esfuerzo es enorme. C1|numbers|Ordinals, apocopation and Roman numerals|500,620,1588,2257,4647,5477,5884,5983,6051,4339|Primer/tercer before masculine nouns; Roman numerals for centuries and monarchs, read as ordinals up to X.|Ordinals (primero, segundo...) behave like adjectives and agree in gender and number.¶• **primero → primer** and **tercero → tercer** before a masculine singular noun: el **primer** momento, mi **primer** triatlón, el **tercer** piso. C1|punct|Commas: connectors, pero, and parenthetical elements|6126,6127,6139,6141,6061,983,1983,3118,4396,5965,6186,6054|Comma after sentence-initial connectors (sin embargo,) and before pero; commas close any inserted element.|Comma use at C1 follows logic more than breath.¶• **Connectors at the start**: put a comma after them. **Sin embargo**, hay excepciones. **No obstante**, el proyecto siguió adelante. **Por consiguiente**, tenemos que replantearnos las cosas. **En cambio**, la segunda opción es más barata. If the connector sits mid-sentence, comma on both sides: La decisión es, **por lo tanto**, acertada.¶• **Before pero, aunque, sino que**: El piso es pequeño**,** pero muy apañado. La historia no se repite**,** pero rima. Not needed before y, o, ni (unless the subjects change).¶• **Inserted elements** (appositions, explanations, vocatives): el fundador, **un hombre discreto**, ... / Lo siento, **Juan**, pero... / Mi vecina, **que es médica**, ... (non-restrictive relative, with commas) versus Los vecinos que hacen ruido se quejan (restrictive: only those neighbours, no commas).¶• **Never separate** subject and verb with a single comma: El resultado de la prueba**,** fue... is wrong.¶• **Lists**: commas between items, y/o/ni without a comma before them (**no Oxford comma**): rojo, verde y azul.¶• **Adverbial clauses first**: Si llueve, nos quedamos. (comma usually before the main clause).¶Tip: English adds a comma before 'and' in long lists or before 'however' differently; Spanish rules are stricter.
C1|punct|Colon, ellipsis, dashes and angle quotes|183,184,197,332,4326,5907,6018,6181,146,262|Colon introduces summaries and quotes; ellipsis for suspense; use « » for quotes and lowercase after a colon.|At C1 you should use punctuation in elegant, formal style.¶• **Colon (:)** introduces an explanation, a list or a quote: Para ir al grano**:** necesitamos más tiempo. Como bien dice el refrán**:** la práctica hace al maestro. After the colon use lowercase, except for proper nouns, quotes and after Querido Juan:. In letters the greeting takes a colon: Estimado señor**:**.¶• **Ellipsis (...)** has three dots, no spaces before, a space after: Si pudiera volver atrás en el tiempo**...** The next word is lowercase if the sentence continues. No fourth dot.¶• **Angle quotes « »** are the standard quotation marks in Spain, with no space inside: Las **«**piedras de la memoria**»** recuerdan a los deportados. Inside quotes use English quotes “ ” and then single ‘ ’. Titles and foreign words go in italics, not quotes.¶• **Dialogue dash (raya —)** opens speech and marks narrator's inserts: —Vámonos —dijo—. (Let's go, he said.) The dash is attached to the word, not floating.¶• **Semicolon (;)** separates long items or balances clauses before connectors: Llegué tarde; sin embargo, entré.¶• **Inverted marks ¿ ¡** start where the question or exclamation begins, not the sentence: Si lo sabes, ¿por qué no lo dices?
C1|style|Formal letters and emails: opening, requests, closing|6319,6320,6321,6322,6333,6334,6335,6337,6340,6343,6353|Formal letters use fixed phrases: Estimada..., Por la presente, Le ruego que, Quedo a su disposición.|Written correspondence has a polished, fixed repertoire. It uses usted and often a formal future or present.¶**Opening:** Estimada señora Schmidt: muchas gracias por su carta. (Dear Mrs Schmidt, thank you for your letter.) En relación con nuestra conversación, le envío la documentación. (With regard to our conversation, I am sending you the documents.)¶**Purpose:** Por la presente, desearía solicitar el puesto anunciado. (I hereby wish to apply for the advertised position.)¶**Bad or good news:** Lamentamos comunicarle que el puesto ya ha sido cubierto. (We regret to inform you that the position has been filled.) Nos complace comunicarle que el puesto es suyo. (We are pleased to tell you the post is yours.)¶**Closing:** Quedo a su disposición para cualquier consulta. (I remain at your disposal for any queries.) A la espera de su respuesta, reciba un cordial saludo. Le agradecemos su confianza.¶Pattern: Lamentamos/Nos complace + comunicarle que. The dative pronoun le is attached to the infinitive.¶Use a colon after the greeting in Spanish, not a comma, and a capital letter only if a new sentence follows.¶Avoid colloquial words; lamentablemente is the usual softener for negative news.
C1|style|Politeness softeners: quisiera, si me lo permite, con todos mis respetos|308,314,315,316,317,318,319,177,300,6177,6347,190|Soften opinions and requests with set phrases such as no quisiera ser indiscreto or con todos mis respetos.|In polite or delicate situations Spanish adds buffers before a request, correction or disagreement.¶• **Quisiera / no quisiera + infinitive** (imperfect subjunctive): No quisiera ser una molestia. (I wouldn't like to be a bother.) Quisiera retomar lo que has dicho. (I would like to come back to what you said.)¶• **Si me lo permite:** Si me lo permite, me gustaría añadir algo. (If you allow me, I'd like to add something.)¶• **Con todos mis respetos / con el debido respeto:** Con todos mis respetos, yo lo veo de otra manera. (With all due respect, I see it differently.)¶• **Si no es indiscreción:** Si no es indiscreción: ¿a qué se dedica? (If it's not indiscreet, what do you do for a living?)¶• **Si te soy sincero / si mal no recuerdo:** Si mal no recuerdo, nos conocimos en Viena. (If I remember correctly, we met in Vienna.)¶Quisiera is more refined than quiero or quería. The formal forms use usted (permítame, disculpe) while friends say Si te soy sincero, No quiero ofenderte, pero...
C1|style|Proverbs and sayings: refranes in conversation|184,593,742,767,768,769,770,771,1594,1596,6274,6277,6280,6282,6283|Spanish refranes are short, rhyming or parallel sayings, often with quien/no + present.|Sayings are part of educated speech. Some are fixed forms with unusual grammar worth recognising.¶• **Quien + present:** Quien se para, se oxida. (If you rest, you rust.) Quien calla, otorga. (Silence implies consent.)¶• **Parallel, rhymed structures:** De tal palo, tal astilla. (Like father, like son.) Dios los cría y ellos se juntan. (Birds of a feather flock together.)¶• **Conditional-free logic:** A buen hambre no hay pan duro. (Hunger is the best sauce.) Ojos que no ven, corazón que no siente. (Out of sight, out of mind.)¶• **Infinitive as noun:** Querer es poder. (Where there's a will there's a way.)¶• **Negative advice:** Zamora no se ganó en una hora. (Rome wasn't built in a day.) Nadie nace sabiendo. (Nobody is born knowing.)¶• **Introduced by a formula:** Como bien dice el refrán: la práctica hace al maestro. (As the saying goes: practice makes perfect.) Bien está lo que bien acaba, como se suele decir.¶Typical features: no article (Barriga llena, corazón contento), word order inverted for rhyme, the subjunctive in relics (Donde hubo fuego, cenizas quedan).¶Use them with a lead-in such as como dice el refrán, ya se sabe, or as se suele decir to sound natural, not overly literary.
C1|style|Attributing opinions and claims: según, dicen que, algunos opinan|3563,5269,5289,4919,5019,2367,1575,335,5485,6339|Attribute views with según, dicen que, algunos opinan que, acusar de; the que-clause is indicative.|To report what people claim without taking responsibility for it, Spanish uses a handful of formulas.¶• **Según + source:** Según los conocimientos actuales, no supone ningún riesgo. (According to current knowledge, it poses no risk.) Según lo acordado, haremos la entrega antes del viernes. (As agreed, we will deliver before Friday.)¶• **Dicen que / dicho / se dice:** El deporte es un asesinato, dicen que dijo Churchill. (Sport is murder, Churchill is said to have said.)¶• **Unos... otros / algunos opinan que:** Algunos opinan que el Estado no debería meterse en la economía. (Some think the state should stay out of the economy.)¶• **Muchos creen que:** Muchos creen que habría que prohibir los vuelos cortos. (Many believe short flights should be banned.)¶• **Verbs of accusation:** La oposición acusa al Gobierno de haber fracasado. (The opposition accuses the government of having failed.)¶In indirect statements with creer, opinar or decir, the que-clause uses the indicative or the conditional for reported ideas; after a negative (No creo que) it needs the subjunctive.¶Backshift is typical when the reporting verb is past: Comentó de pasada que se mudaba (or se muda if still true).
